title: A class of sum Hessian quotient equations arising in conformal geometry
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence result of $(n-1)$-admissible solutions to a class of sum Hessian quotient equations with the modified Schouten tensor on Riemannian manifolds. By establishing uniform a priori estimates, we prove the solvability of the problem via degree theory.

title: Quantum Color Newton Rings
abstract: We study integral Newton rings attached to symmetric quantum colors. We show that their boundary values at a deleted node are exactly the elements of Habiro's cyclotomic completion, and we describe their quantum neighborhoods at $q=1$ uniformly in the rank. The symmetric-color $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ invariants of a knot are the values of an element of such a ring. In its expansion at $q=1$, the coefficient of $(q-1)^m$ has denominator dividing the $(n-1+2m)$th power of the Alexander polynomial, with integral numerator, and this exponent is sharp. For $5_2$ and $6_1$ at $q=i$, the period matrices of the rank-two coefficient recurrences have spectral modules of exact order three in the Picard group of an affine elliptic curve.

title: Non-simply connected Poincaré surgery
abstract: We give homotopy-theoretic proofs of the principal results of non-simply connected Poincaré surgery. These include the Fundamental Theorem of Poincaré surgery, the Poincaré transversality exact sequence, and the construction of Poincaré handle structures. All results apply in dimensions~$\ge 8$.

title: Nonlinear neighborhoods of smooth curves and arbitrarily negative Wahl defects
abstract: We develop a theory of nonlinear neighborhoods of smooth projective curves of genus at least two, constructed by gluing products of open subsets of a curve with a disc using nonlinear changes of the disc coordinate. Their zero sections have normal bundles of negative degree and contract to normal surface singularities. For the minimal good resolution \((X,E) \to (V,0)\) of a normal complex surface singularity other than a rational double point, the Wahl defect is defined by \(Δ(V,0) := h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)-h^1(S_X)+h^1(\bigwedge^2S_X)\), where \(E\) is reduced and \(S_X = Θ_X(-\log E)\). We give a finite formula for this defect in terms of extension obstructions when \(E\) is a single smooth curve. For our constructed neighborhoods, the formula involves extensions of functions alone, includes obstructions at every order, and gives a sharp lower bound depending only on the genus. We apply the theory to hyperelliptic curves and smooth plane curves. Both families consist of singularities that are neither \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein nor quasi-homogeneous. The hyperelliptic examples realize every nonpositive integer as a Wahl defect and attain the genus bound in every genus at least two. They disprove Wahl's Main Conjecture, which asserts nonnegativity for non-Gorenstein singularities, with equality precisely in the quasi-homogeneous case.

title: Exotic diffeomorphisms on closed aspherical $4$-manifolds
abstract: We study a class of diffeomorphisms of closed manifolds obtained from Davis' reflection trick construction, which are obtained by reflecting a diffeomorphism supported in the fundamental chamber of such a manifold. We use this construction to exhibit the first examples of closed aspherical $4$-manifolds with diffeomorphisms that are topologically isotopic to the identity map, but not smoothly isotopic to it.

title: A Proof of the Area Vanishing Square Peg Conjecture
abstract: We resolve an open problem posed by Tao related to the Toeplitz square peg conjecture. We prove that four simple closed polygonal curves in the cylinder, each winding once in the positive direction, jointly inscribe a square whenever the alternating sum of their $\int y\, dx$ integrals vanishes. The proof reduces the problem to the non-displaceability of a pair of Lagrangian tori, which we establish using Lagrangian Floer homology.

title: Exact Endpoint Asymptotics and Almost-Sure Limits for Uniform Empirical Measures in Two Dimensions
abstract: For the empirical measure of the first $n$ points of one infinite sequence of independent uniform samples in the unit square, we identify the leading constant in the bounded-Lipschitz distance to area measure, equivalently in $W_1$, both in expectation and almost surely along all sample sizes. The constant is $c_*=κ_1/(2\sqrtπ)\in(0,1/4]$, where $κ_1$ is the linear-growth Gaussian variational constant of Armegioiu--Goldman--Grotto--Trevisan. This answers the two-dimensional bounded-Lipschitz convergence question posed by Yukich in 1989. We give the complete endpoint argument, square--torus comparison, empirical reduction, and full-sequence probability argument.

title: Infinitely many closed geodesic images on simply connected compact rank-one symmetric spaces
abstract: We prove that every smooth Riemannian metric on the underlying smooth manifold of a simply connected compact rank-one symmetric space, namely $S^n$ $(n\ge2)$, $\CP^m$ $(m\ge1)$, $\HP^m$ $(m\ge1)$, or $\OP^2$ admits infinitely many geometrically distinct prime closed geodesics. Here a prime closed geodesic is a nonconstant closed geodesic which is not an iterate of a shorter one, and geometric distinctness means that the images in the manifold are pairwise different. Thus iterating a geodesic, changing its starting point, or reversing its orientation does not count as a new geodesic. No nondegeneracy assumption on the metric is imposed. These manifolds have bounded loop-space Betti numbers, so the usual homological growth criterion does not yield this conclusion. We use the length filtration together with rotation and reversal of loops. A controlled cut construction gives a uniform filling estimate in the based loop space, with a fixed increase in length independent of degree, which we transfer to free loops. We then calculate global equivariant classes associated with odd and even iterates. Assuming finitely many prime geodesic images forces incompatible requirements at a class's first critical level. The proof treats spheres and projective spaces within a common framework and does not assume a sphere infinitude theorem.

title: CM Elliptic Analogue of the Coleman--Ihara Formula
abstract: The Soulé characters are Kummer characters constructed from cyclotomic units and also arising from the Galois action on the pro-$p$ geometric fundamental group of $\mathbb{P}^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$. The Coleman--Ihara formula describes the restrictions of these characters to the local Galois group at $p$ as products of the Coates--Wiles homomorphisms and Kubota--Leopoldt $p$-adic $L$-values at positive odd integers. In this paper, we prove an elliptic analogue of this formula for elliptic curves with complex multiplication by the ring of integers of an imaginary quadratic field $K$. We consider certain Kummer characters associated with elliptic units, which we call elliptic Soulé characters. These characters are elliptic counterparts of the classical Soulé characters and also arise from the Galois action on the pro-$p$ geometric fundamental groups of once-punctured elliptic curves. For suitable pairs of positive integers $(i,j)$, we give an explicit description of their restrictions to the relevant local Galois groups as products of the two-variable Coates--Wiles homomorphisms introduced by Yager and the two-variable $p$-adic $L$-values of $K$.

title: On the Last-Iterate Convergence of Clipped Gradient Methods
abstract: In stochastic (strongly) convex optimization, establishing last-iterate convergence guarantees for first-order methods has recently garnered increasing attention, as this not only deepens the theoretical understanding of these algorithms but also aligns more closely with practice. Notably, people have demonstrated that one of the most famous, simple, and popular methods, Stochastic Gradient Descent ($\mathtt{SGD}$), provably achieves last-iterate convergence. However, the existing results may have limited applicability, since they typically rely on strong conditions on the gradient noise (e.g., an exponentially decaying tail) rather than the more realistic heavy-tailed noise. Unfortunately, when faced with heavy-tailed noise, $\mathtt{SGD}$ is known to exhibit undesirable behavior or even fail to converge. To address the challenge of heavy-tailed noise, people have proposed $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$, an algorithm that combines $\mathtt{SGD}$ with a simple mechanism, gradient clipping. Although $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$ performs well in practice, its last-iterate convergence property remains highly underexplored. In this work, we prove the first optimal last-iterate rates in high probability for $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$ under heavy-tailed noise, thereby closing a gap in the literature.

title: Crossing numbers of simplicial complexes
abstract: This paper studies crossing numbers of $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes drawn in $\mathbb R^{2d}$ or $\mathbb S^{2d}$. We clarify and generalize a number of known results and conjectures from the graph case to higher dimensions: the crossing lemma (including the exceptional case of two-dimensional complexes drawn in dimension $4$), a generalized Harary-Hill conjecture (and evidence for it), existence of a midrange crossing constant (in a weak sense), and upper bound constructions based on stochastic geometry (related to Sylvester's problem) and the cyclic polytope. Some of our results are new even in the case of graphs: we give a simple proof of the Harary-Hill conjecture for antipodal drawings, and sharpen the threshold above which the rectilinear and spherical crossing numbers of the Erdős-Rényi random graph behave like those of the complete graph.

title: Operator Algebraic Quantum Hypergroups
abstract: We develop a theory of operator algebraic quantum hypergroups and their representations, formulated using a special case of the algebraic quantum hypergroup framework of van Daele and Delvaux. As part of the axioms, every operator algebraic quantum hypergroup admits a dual object of the same type. We prove that a certain universal completion in the compact case satisfies the axioms of an earlier notion of a compact quantum hypergroup in the sense of the second author and Chapovsky. As part of this theory, we discuss their (co)amenability properties. We consider examples induced by conditional expectations of algebraic quantum groups satisfying certain properties, which include quantum hypergroups corresponding to double cosets and automorphisms of quantum groups, and quantum hypergroups induced by representation categories of Kac type compact quantum groups.

title: Length control for foliations by Jordan curves via smooth quasiconformal maps
abstract: Let $Ω\subsetneq\mathbb C$ be a non-empty simply connected domain and $0<p<2$. Bouchala and Koskela [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (2024)] proved that there exists a quasiconformal map $f:\mathbb D\toΩ$ such that $\int_0^1\ell(f(r S^1))^p\,dr<\infty$, and asked whether this conclusion holds at $p=2$, or even for every $0<p<2+\varepsilon$ with some $\varepsilon>0$. We answer this question affirmatively with $\varepsilon=2/157$ by constructing a single smooth $5$-quasiconformal map $f:\mathbb D\toΩ$ satisfying this integrability condition simultaneously for every $0<p<2+2/157$.

title: $λ$-geodesic convexity of the squared sliced-Wasserstein distance
abstract: The squared Wasserstein distance with respect to a fixed target measure is not a convex function along Wasserstein geodesics over $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $d\geq 2$. Still, in dimension $d=1$, this function is $2$-geodesically convex. We prove that the square of the sliced-Wasserstein distance (which is a distance constructed averaging one-dimensional Wasserstein distances) is $λ$-geodesically convex (possibly with $λ\leq 0$) on sets of measures satisfying upper bounds on their density, when the target measure satisfies some given geometric conditions. We also present some consequences of this result in the study of the sliced-Wasserstein flow.

title: Emergence of partially hyperbolic skew-products with circle fibers
abstract: We study the statistical behavior of partially hyperbolic skew-products over Axiom A diffeomorphisms using emergence. Generically, these systems satisfy the Palis conjecture: they have a finite number of physical measures whose basins together have full volume. In particular, for Lebesgue almost every point, the empirical measures converge to one of finitely many physical measures. We study the non-generic case and prove that, even when the sequence of empirical measures may have uncountably many accumulation points, these systems have low emergence.

title: Learning Warm Starts for the Simplex Method from Measured Solver Cost
abstract: Learned warm starts for the simplex method build starting bases using predictions of which variables will be basic at optimality. Prior work has shown that starting bases predicted by graph neural networks can sharply reduce iteration counts, but the time saved may fall well short of the iterations saved. On 25 classes of linear programs (LPs), we find that a strong supervised basis predictor removes two thirds of the dual simplex's iterations but only a third of its time. Two effects explain the gap: the iterations removed by a good start tend to be cheap, and closeness to an optimal basis does not rank starts by cost. We prove that two starts with equal overlap with an optimal basis and equal pivot counts can differ in linear-algebra work by a factor that grows with the square root of the number of rows. Empirically, across the starts of one LP, the pivot count explains 71% of the variance of log solve time, while the CPU instruction count explains 98.5%. We introduce CostStart, which uses supervised prediction for the basis and trains a small policy on measured instruction counts to choose, per LP, how many predicted columns to use, which algorithm and pricing rule to run, and whether to warm-start at all. On unseen LPs of the training classes, including LPs four times the training size, CostStart roughly halves the solve time relative to the solver's default start and is 1.4 to 2.2 times as fast as two published methods retrained on the same data.

title: The $A^A$ problem for finite ordered sets
abstract: For ordered sets $X$ and $Y$, let $Y^X$ denote the ordered set of order-preserving maps from $X$ to $Y$, ordered pointwise. In 1984, D. Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ forces $A\cong B$ when $A$ and $B$ are finite ordered sets. We prove that it does. The proof combines direct decompositions with an auxiliary ordering of connected ordered sets and a careful choice of intervals of maximum height. We then extend the reconstruction result to several forms of repeated exponentiation.

title: Characterizations in terms of Generalized Inverses
abstract: Using simply outer inverse and their differences, we characterize many known classes of rings including von Neumann regular, unit-regular, exchange, clean, and strongly clean rings.

title: Radon measures in the Berkovich space and generically stable measures in ACVF
abstract:
In this paper we study Keisler measures in models of ACVF. We give analogue definitions for a Keisler measure to be orthogonal to the value group and stably dominated using unique extensions, in the spirit of invariant types. Our first theorem shows that a global $M$-invariant Keisler measure is generically stable if and only if it is orthogonal to the value group if and only if it is stably dominated. This theorem is later applied to prove that for a projective variety $X$ defined over a spherically complete model $M$ of ACVF whose value group is $\mathbb R$, there is a one-to-one correspondance between the generically stable measures centered on $X$ and the Radon measures on its Berkovich analyfication of $X$. Such theorem is a measure-theoretic extension of the celebrated work of Hrushovski-Loeser, which establishes a correspondence between generically stable types with the points of the Berkovich analyfication $X^{an}$ of a projective variety$X$.
  As an application, normalized Chambert-Loir measures associated with semipositive continuous metrics naturally give rise examples of generically stable Keisler measures.

title: Explicit reduced APN permutations: ramification and optimal Galois-ring lifts
abstract: Let $m\ge5$ be odd and $q=2^m$. For every odd $r$ with $3\le r<m$ and $\gcd(r,m)=1$ we give the reduced polynomial $P_{m,r}=\mathrm{red}((T_r^3)^{2^{m-2}})$, $T_r=\sum_{i<r}X^{2^i}$, explicitly: it has coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_2$ and exactly $3r-2$ terms, it is an APN permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$, and its formal derivative $1+X^{2^{r-2}}+X^{2^{m-2}}$ has no zero on $\mathbb{F}_q$ and is two-to-one. We determine the ramification of $P_{m,r}$ as a map of the projective line for all admissible $(m,r)$: there are $2^{m-r}$ finite ramification points, all wild, with index and different exponent $2^{r-2}$, all over the single finite branch value $1$. The $0/1$ lift of $P_{m,r}$ satisfies an identity in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ that evaluates it over every Galois ring $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ with $m-1$ squarings, one general multiplication and $r+5$ additions or subtractions. For every quadratic optimal APN permutation $p$ of $\mathbb{F}_q$ (in particular $P_{m,r}$), every $k\ge2$ and every coefficient lift $F$ of $p$ to $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$, we determine the differential rows of $F$ exactly in the unit directions whose residue lies outside the kernel $\{0,ρ\}$ of the linear part of $p'$ (they are the residue rows of $p$; $ρ=1$ for $P_{m,r}$) and in the directions in $2^{k-1}\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)\setminus\{0\}$ (every nonzero entry equals $2q^{k-1}$). We also give a self-contained proof of the Li--Wang criterion for a Gold function plus a linearised polynomial, which explains why the inner map of $P_{m,r}$ is not a monomial, and record a two-word, two-layer transition that a simple linear layer forbids at the residue level.

title: Conditional limit laws for open intermittent dynamics
abstract: We obtain conditional limit theorems for open intermittent Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti (LSV) maps. Unlike the results of closed systems (e.g. some uniformly expanding maps), we obtain a new limit distribution, which is different from the Gaussian law or the stable law, for both "regular" and singular observables.

title: Four-Level Quantized Soft Information Aided Hard-Decision Decoder for Product-like Codes
abstract: We propose a novel low-complexity soft-aided hard-decision decoding scheme for product-like codes, termed iterative bounded-distance decoding (iBDD) with graded scaled reliability and bit-flipping (GSRF). This scheme operates on four-level quantized soft information. It incorporates a graded scaled reliability rule to assign decoding confidence to the bounded-distance decoding result, and employs a bit-flipping rule based on bit-level and component-code-level reliability. A selective re-decoding rule is designed to further facilitate the error performance while keeping the number of BDD attempts in reasonably low levels. The decoding parameter design of iBDD-GSRF is investigated for product codes and staircase codes, respectively. Simulation results on both codes verify that iBDD-GSRF achieves a gain of more than 0.4 dB over the conventional iBDD, comparable to several existing unquantized soft-aided decoders.

title: Positivity of Wahl defects and representations from index-one covers
abstract: Let \((X,E) \to (V,0)\) be the minimal good resolution of a normal complex surface singularity, with \(E\) reduced. The Wahl defect is \(Δ(V,0) :=h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)-h^1(S_X)+h^1(\bigwedge^2 S_X)\), where \(S_X=Θ_X(-\log E)\). For non-Gorenstein \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein singularities \((V,0)\), we prove that \(Δ(V,0)\geq0\), with equality precisely in the quasi-homogeneous case. This proves Wahl's Main Conjecture in this class and his \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein and Rational Conjectures. The proof expresses \(Δ\) as the multiplicity of the canonical character in a representation constructed from differential forms and residues. We also prove \(Δ+4p_g\geq0\) for arbitrary normal surface singularities, with equality precisely for rational quasi-homogeneous singularities. For smoothings of rational surface singularities, we give a Riemann--Roch formula for the lengths of the cokernels of the restriction maps to the central fiber for all reflexive canonical powers, in terms of the Milnor number and periodic local Riemann--Roch corrections. This yields numerical and representation-theoretic criteria for \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein smoothings, defined as quotients of equivariant smoothings of the index-one cover with trivial group action on the base. If a rational singularity admits a \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein smoothing, such smoothings are precisely those with minimal Milnor number, or equivalently those whose smoothing components have minimal dimension. Combining these results, we prove that every rational homology disk smoothing is \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein, has a rational weighted homogeneous central fiber, and occurs over a one-dimensional smoothing component. Together with the known weighted homogeneous classification, this completes the analytic classification of normal surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings.

title: Adaptive Randomized Neural Networks for PDEs: Structure-Aware Feature Redistribution and Residual-Driven Block Enrichment
abstract: Randomized neural networks retain an output-linear least-squares solve, but globally sampled random features may fail to capture the spatial and scale structure of PDE solutions. We propose SFRBE--RaNN, a two-stage adaptive trial-space construction. SFR redistributes a fixed feature budget according to regional indicator masses and adapts regional weight scales through low-dimensional residual-based optimization. RBE constructs nonredundant enrichments by screening multiple activation families, removing represented response directions, and selecting the smallest admissible prefix. For solution-dependent operators, candidates are screened with a frozen operator and accepted only after nonlinear residual verification. For fixed linear problems, we establish an exact discrete residual-reduction identity and a conditional solution-error estimate. Building on this identity, we combine safeguarded SFR with RBE capture factors to derive a finite-horizon error bound involving baseline best approximation and empirical consistency, together with a conditional random-search success-probability bound. Numerical experiments on localized, multiscale, and nonlinear space--time problems demonstrate the method's effectiveness.

title: Linear bounds for rich-neighbor edge-colorings
abstract: An edge in a proper edge-coloring is rich if all edges adjacent to it receive pairwise distinct colors. A rich-neighbor edge-coloring is a proper edge-coloring in which every non-isolated edge is adjacent to a rich edge. The rich-neighbor chromatic index $\rn(G)$ is the minimum number of colors in such a coloring. We prove that every loopless multigraph $G$ satisfies $\rn(G)\le3χ'(G)$, where $χ'(G)$ is the chromatic index. Exact values are also determined for complete bipartite graphs and complete graphs. For all positive integers $m,n$, $\rn(K_{m,n})=m+n-1$, except that $\rn(K_{2,2})=4$. For $n\ge3$, $\rn(K_n)=2n-3$, except that $\rn(K_4)=6$ and $\rn(K_6)=10$. Moreover, for $n\ge7$, the rich edges in every optimal rich-neighbor edge-coloring of $K_n$ form a star forest.

title: Automorphisms of twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2E_6$ over local rings
abstract: We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2E_6$ over commutative local rings with involution and $2$ invertible, for both isogeny types. Every automorphism is standard, with no invertibility assumption on $3$. In the adjoint case, it has a unique expression as a composition of conjugation by an element of the full twisted group and a ring automorphism commuting with the involution. For the simply connected form, the full group equals its elementary subgroup, and the factors are strictly inner, diagonal, and ring automorphisms. The main step replaces a linear change of basis by a group element. Invariant alternating tensors determine the transported Chevalley bracket. We correct this bracket over a faithfully flat local extension and descend the resulting conjugating element by uniqueness. Root-subgroup relations then recover the coefficient automorphism.

title: Competitive displacement in the grass-bushes-trees process on a scale-free network
abstract: The grass-bushes-trees process is a two-type contact process in which the types face asymmetric birth mechanisms. Vertices of a graph can either be occupied by a tree, occupied by a bush, or empty (containing grass). The trees die with rate $1$ and give birth with rate $λ_{\mathcal T}$ on any neighbouring vertex (possibly taking the place of a bush). Bushes die with rate $1$ and give birth with rate $λ_{\mathcal B}$ on any empty neighbouring vertex; in particular, they are forbidden from taking the place of trees. We study this process on a power law random graph, namely the erased configuration model. We study which graph parameters lead to the possibility of coexistence versus the necessity of competitive displacement, i.e. joint metastability or fast extinction of the bushes.

title: A Coupled Fluid Naghdi Shell Windkessel Model for Pulmonary Artery Banding: Partitioned Numerical Scheme and Parameter Estimation
abstract:
We develop a 3D fluid structure interaction model for blood flow through deformable vessels with localized constrictions, motivated by pulmonary artery banding in neonates with congenital heart disease. The model couples incompressible Navier Stokes equations in an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian framework with a Naghdi shell model for the arterial wall and a three element Windkessel model for downstream circulation. The shell describes a 3D cylindrical vessel wall with variable radius and is defined on a 2D reference domain. Its low regularity formulation retains membrane, bending, and transverse shear deformation while requiring only first derivatives of the reference midsurface, accommodating piecewise smooth geometries with discontinuous surface slopes.
  We derive the coupled variational formulation and develop a non-iterative partitioned scheme with a Robin-type interface condition incorporating arterial wall inertia. For a linearized fixed domain problem, we establish a discrete energy estimate under suitable assumptions. A unscented Kalman filter estimates proximal and distal resistances and compliance from inlet-pressure observations. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent pressure wave propagation and wall deformation under spatial and temporal refinement. Comparisons of the standard Naghdi shell and a modified, predominantly radial shell model reveal how structural deformation mechanisms affect wave speed and displacement. An idealized pulmonary artery banding example demonstrates the coupled fluid shell Windkessel model with parameter estimation. The framework enables investigation of the hemodynamic and mechanical effects of localized constrictions and their dependence on downstream vascular properties.

title: $q_x$-Bass Martingales: Optimality, Existence and Convergence
abstract: We introduce the class of $q_x$-Bass martingales, extending the notion of $q$-Bass martingales. These are martingale couplings with prescribed marginals whose transition kernels are closest to a given family of reference kernels $(q_x)_{x \in \mathbb R^d}$ in the sense of a suitable weak optimal transport problem. We show that $q_x$-Bass martingales are optimizers of this problem and establish a strong duality result. Building on this duality, we introduce an algorithm for their computation and, under compactness assumptions on the prescribed marginals, prove its convergence, thereby establishing existence. We then specialize to one-dimensional marginals and show that the algorithm reduces to a fixed-point iteration.

title: Ehrhart Polynomials of Triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$
abstract: We present two ways of constructing Ehrhart polynomials corresponding to certain triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$. One of our methods employs Popoviciu's Theorem, while the other method uses a version of Pick's Theorem adapted to rank-2 lattices in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We then apply our methods to linear Diophantine equations of the form $ax+by+cz=n$ and develop upper and lower bounds on the number of solutions in nonnegative integers $x$, $y$, and $z$. The bounds we develop are closed form quasi-polynomials, and the difference between them is bounded by a constant depending only on $a$ and $b$. As an application, we prove that the $k$th Frobenius number exists for any triple of positive integers and any $k$.

title: Radiation Conditions and Uniqueness Theorems for Open Wave-guide Networks
abstract: We state radiation conditions and prove a variety of uniqueness theorem for models of wave-guide networks, including acoustic wave-guide networks, and electromagnetic wave-guide networks described by the time harmonic Maxwell equations. To analyze Maxwell wave-guide networks we need to establish generalizations of the Mourre estimates from [29, 32].

title: $L^\infty$-regularity thresholds for a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation: dispersive blow-up vs. nonlinear stability
abstract: We study a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation arising in the mean-field description of exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensates. The dynamics close to macroscopic wave functions $r_0e^{iω_0 t +ik_0x}$ is governed by a stabilizing relaxation mechanism without suppressing dispersive blow-up. We show that this competition yields $L^\infty$-regularity thresholds. More precisely, we construct solutions for which arbitrarily small perturbations from $C^4_b$ can develop finite time blow-up in $C^3_b$ whereas perturbations from $C^{4+η}_b$ for every $η>0$, satisfy a global-in-time $C^3_b$-stability estimate. The stability analysis is carried out in modulation spaces $M_{\infty,1}^k$.

title: Linear Independence of Polynomial Compositions with Bounded Input Degree
abstract: We prove the weak composition-independence conjectures of Kohn, Marchetti, Massarenti and Mella. The proof uses deformations of rational curves and a single kernel of the linearized equation. Riemann-Roch gives a contradiction from tangent fields with controlled poles. By settling these conjectures, we prove that a neural network with a general polynomial activation function of sufficiently large degree is identifiable.

title: Two Short Proofs of the $A^A$ Theorem
abstract:
In 1984, D.~Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ implies $A\cong B$ for finite, nonempty ordered sets $A$ and~$B$. J.\,D. Farley and the author proved that it does.
  In this paper, we give two short proofs using all intervals of maximum height and the elements with exactly one lower cover. The first proof averages over these intervals; the second takes their disjoint sum and constructs three invariants. Both avoid the auxiliary ordering, direct factorization, and canonical coordinates of the earlier proof.

title: Precise Asymptotics for Dense High-Dimensional Huber Regression under Heteroscedasticity
abstract: We study Huber regression in a heteroscedastic linear model in the proportional regime $n/p \to δ\in (1, \infty)$. Our main result is an exact characterization of the asymptotic empirical distribution of the Huber estimator. This characterization is in terms of three scalar parameters which determine the first-order centre and the asymptotic variance of the Huber estimator. The result shows that with heteroscedastic noise, the first-order centre may contain an additional component along the variance index coefficient. We derive the displacement coefficients that determine this centre, as well as the exact asymptotic variance. The analysis uses the matrix approximate message passing (AMP) framework to jointly track the regression and variance index coefficients, extending the existing framework for homoscedastic M-estimators. We illustrate the implications of this characterization by constructing a test for centre displacement and examining its empirical size and power through simulations.

title: Mixed moment and joint non-vanishing of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(1)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(1)$ $L$-functions
abstract: In this article, we study the mixed-moment problem for the product of central values of two $L$-functions twisted by a Dirichlet character of large conductor $q$. Precisely, for a fixed $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ Hecke-Maass cusp form $π$, we asymptotically evaluate the first moment, with $\textit{power-saving}$ error term for the product of central $L$-values $L(1/2, π\timesχ)\overline{L(1/2, χ)}$ averaged over the $\textit{full family}$ $\{χ\,(\mathrm{mod}\,{q}): Q\leq q\leq 2Q\}$ of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q$. And as a consequence, we also established the simultaneous non-vanishing of the aforementioned central $L$-values.

title: Variance-Feedback Noise in Interacting Diffusions: Shape Dynamics and Mean-Field Limits
abstract: We study a system of $N$ attractive interacting diffusions where the variance feeds back into the noise. That is the common and idiosyncratic Brownian forcing has amplitude $κ(S_t^N)^q$, with $S_t^N$ the empirical variance of the system, $κ>0$ and $q\geq 0$. With the interaction kernel given by $K(z)=|z|^p z$, for $p\geq 0$, feedback through the empirical variance gives the system critical homogeneity at $q=(p+2)/4$. For this exponent an intrinsic time change separates the variance from the normalized centered configuration: the latter evolves autonomously on a unit sphere and, when it is not purely driven by common noise and the sphere has positive dimension, is a reversible elliptic diffusion with an explicit invariant Gibbs measure. In this case, for $p>0$, the stationary averaged dissipation gives an exact finite-particle trichotomy between consensus, recurrent excursions through arbitrarily small and large variance scales, and finite-time explosion. At critical homogeneity we also derive an autonomous unit-variance mean-field equation and its constrained free-energy dissipation identity. Across the subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes, we establish well-posedness and boundary classifications and prove conditional propagation of chaos on intervals where the limiting solution is unique and nonexplosive. We connect the sharp finite-particle coercivity constants to a mean-field variational problem. Finite-size Itô corrections enlarge the universal coercive consensus region. We solve the linear model, where $p=0$, completely, including invariant laws, explosion probabilities, noncommuting limits, and an $N^{-1/2}$ transition window.

title: 86 unknowns for Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals
abstract: Recently, Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers was solved negatively by OpenAI based on a five-contact height estimate and a pole-parity construction. In this paper, we prove further that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial $f(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})$ with integer coefficients whether the equation $f(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})=0$ has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{86}\in\mathbb Q$.

title: The real Betti realization of very effective Hermitian K-theory
abstract: Real Betti realization is a symmetric monoidal functor from the category of motivic spectra to that of topological spectra, extending the functor that associates to a scheme over $\mathbb{R}$ the space of its real points. In this article, we identify the $\mathcal{E}_1$-ring structure on the real realization of $\mathsf{ko}$, the very effective cover of Hermitian K-theory $\mathsf{KO}$, by an explicit 2-local fracture square, as being equivalent to $\mathsf{L}(\mathbb{R})_{\geq 0}$, the connective L-theory spectrum of $\mathbb{R}$. Along the way, we also compute the real realization of other motivic ring spectra: motivic cohomology $\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}/2$, the variant $\widetilde{\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$, $\mathsf{KO}$, the very effective cover $\mathsf{kgl}$ of algebraic K-theory $\mathsf{KGL}$.

title: Connectivity and Diameter of Friends and Strangers Graphs Using Minimum Degree
abstract: Given graphs $X,Y$ on $n$ vertices, Defant and Kravitz defined the friends and strangers graph, denoted $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$. The vertices of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ are bijections $σ:V(X)\to V(Y)$, and two bijections $σ$ and $σ'$ are adjacent in $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ if they differ by a transposition $(ab)$ such that $a$ and $b$ are adjacent in $X$ and $σ(a)$ and $σ(b)$ are adjacent in $Y$. Our main result resolves a conjecture of Bangachev that if $X,Y$ are connected graphs and $2\min\{δ(X),δ(Y)\}+3\max\{δ(X),δ(Y)\}\ge 3n$, then $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is connected. The main step in the proof is showing that there exists an absolute constant $C$ such that for any adjacent vertices $a,b\in V(X)$ and any vertex $σ\in V(\mathrm{FS}(X,Y))$, $a$ and $b$ can swap positions in at most $C$ moves. Furthermore, we prove that if $X,Y$ are connected graphs satisfying the above minimum degree condition, then the diameter of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is $O(n^2/\min\{δ(X),δ(Y)\})$, and that this is sharp as a bound on the maximum diameter of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ in this regime. This work improves the diameter results of Akella and Li, and resolves many of their questions. Moreover, we show that even for disconnected graphs $X$ and $Y$, the same minimum degree condition implies that the diameter of any connected component of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is $O(n^2)$.

title: Low-rank perturbation of symplectic matrices
abstract: In this paper the generic behavior of the Jordan structure of symplectic matrices under low-rank structure-preserving transformations is considered. So far, only the case of rank-one perturbations was covered in the literature, and this result is now extended to the case of arbitrary rank $k$. As a key step toward the main result, it is shown that all symplectic matrices that differ from the identity by rank $k$ can be represented as a product of $k$ symplectic reflectors unless they are similar to a diagonalizable matrix having only the eigenvalues $\pm 1$.

title: Oka-Weil approximation theorem for polynomials with exponents in compact convex sets in $\mathbb R^n$
abstract: Let $S\subset\R^n_+$ be a compact convex set with $0\in S$, and let $\cP^S$ be the ring of polynomials whose exponents of the $m$-th degree lie in the dilates $mS$. Sigurðardóttir proved an Oka--Weil theorem for compact $\cP^S$-convex subsets of $(\C^*)^n$ and asked whether it holds for all compact $\cP^S$-convex subsets of $\C^n$. We answer this question affirmatively when the cone $\R_+S$ is rational polyhedral, for every $S$ when $n=2$, and for several classes of nonpolyhedral cones in all dimensions; in all these cases the compact sets may meet the coordinate hyperplanes. For arbitrary $S$ we prove that the Oka--Weil property of a compact $\cP^S$-convex set is equivalent to the compactness of its hull with respect to a finitely generated monomial subring of $\cP^S$, to a corona-type certificate, and to the existence of a bounded neighbourhood defined by finitely many inequalities $|p_j|<c_j$ with $p_j\in\cP^S$. The proofs use monomial charts, the classical Oka--Weil theorem in an auxiliary affine space, and elementary Gelfand theory. As applications we obtain an Oka--Stolzenberg criterion for $\cP^S$-hulls and the corresponding rational approximation theorem.

title: Random Quotients of Hyperbolic Spaces with Respect to WPD Actions and Linear Connectivity of the Boundary
abstract: We study random quotients of acylindrically hyperbolic groups and hierchically hyperbolic groups, whose (partial) hyperbolicity is captured by their actions on Gromov hyperbolic spaces. We show that if an acylindrically hyperbolic group $G$ acts on a Gromov hyperbolic space $X$ coarsely transitively with a WPD element, then the quotient of $X$ by the normal closure of a random element of $G$ has linearly connected boundary. If $G$ is a group with a (relative) hierarchically hyperbolic group structure, with a quasi-tree top domain $X$, then in fact the quotient of $X$ by the normal closure of a random element of $G$ has boundary homeomorphic to the Nöbeling curve.

title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
abstract: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.

title: Normal complex surface singularities with rational homology disk smoothings
abstract: We prove that a normal surface singularity whose minimal good resolution graph has at least two nodes does not admit a rational homology disk smoothing. Together with the earlier graph classifications and the analytic classifications of Fowler and Wahl, this gives a complete classification of normal surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings and proves Wahl's conjecture. The same argument also proves Wahl's Rational Conjecture.

title: A One-Sided McDiarmid-Type Inequality for Heavy Tails via Reverse KL Tensorization
abstract: We revisit McDiarmid's inequality, a central tool in statistical learning theory and algorithm analysis. We show that large deviations above the mean are exponentially unlikely for functions of independent random variables that are almost surely bounded above and satisfy a conditional moment assumption of order $p\in(1,2]$. When $p<2$, the result applies even when the function has infinite variance. Our proof relies on a new tensorization inequality for the Kullback--Leibler divergence, termed reverse KL tensorization, which may be of independent interest. Applications include concentration of the sample mean and median-of-means estimator, and one-sided uniform risk bounds for unbounded losses.

title: A simpler proof that there are no Landau--Siegel zeros
abstract: This paper simplifies the recent OpenAI proof that there are no Landau--Siegel zeros.

title: Superfast Spectral Compressed Sensing with Quadratic Convergence
abstract: In this paper, we study the spectral compressed sensing problem of recovering a spectrally sparse signal from linear compressive measurements. Exploiting the low-rank Hankel structure associated with the signal, we formulate a nonconvex fixed-rank optimization problem with a Hankel regularization. We propose a Superfast Iterative Hard Thresholding (SIHT) algorithm, where each iteration consists of a tangent-space least-squares update followed by a fixed-rank hard thresholding projection. SIHT is the first nonconvex algorithm with provable quadratic convergence for spectral compressed sensing. For random Gaussian measurements, it achieves exact recovery in the noiseless case and stable recovery in the noisy case with near-optimal sample complexity. To efficiently implement SIHT, we develop a parameterized conjugate gradient method for solving the least-squares subproblem, endowing SIHT with state-of-the-art computational and memory efficiency. Numerical experiments are provided to validate our results.

title: A $p$-adic Riemann--Hilbert correspondence over Robba rings
abstract: We construct overconvergent period sheaves $\mathcal{O}\widetilde{\mathbb{C}}^{I,\dagger}$ and $\mathcal{O}\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^{\dagger,+}$ on the $v$-site of a liftable semi-stable formal scheme $\mathfrak{X}_Z$. By establishing a decompletion theorem for small representations, we prove a $p$-adic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence relating small $\widetilde{\mathbb{C}}^I$-local systems (resp. $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-local systems) on the generic fiber $X_Z$ to small flat connections on the associated period ringed spaces. We further analyze the local Frobenius action and show that this correspondence is compatible with the Frobenius structure. As an application, we prove a comparison theorem between the cohomology of these period sheaves and the rigid cohomology of the special fiber, refining results of Le Bras and Colmez--Nizioł.

title: A counterexample to a conjecture of Plotnick on knot exteriors
abstract: We resolve a conjecture of S. Plotnick from 1983 concerning the homotopy type of four-dimensional knot complements. We show that the exteriors of two branched twist spins of the trefoil, which were shown by Plotnick not to be homotopy equivalent as boundary pairs and hence not homeomorphic, are in fact simple homotopy equivalent. The main ingredient of the proof is the construction of an explicit element of augmentation $49$ in the integral group ring of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_5)$ which is a unit modulo the group norm and commutes with the element inducing the monodromy on the fundamental group.

title: Skew fields of non-commutative meromorphic functions affiliated to finite operator algebras
abstract:
We embed skew fields of meromorphic functions in several non-commuting variables into the topological $*-$algebra of closed linear operators affiliated to a finite von Neumann algebra, $\mathfrak{M}$, with faithful, normal tracial state, $τ$. Namely, let $\mathscr{O} _d (r)$, $r \in (0, +\infty]$, denote the rings of formal power series in $d \in \mathbb{N}$ non-commuting variables with ``radius of convergence" at least $r$ and let $Ξ\in \mathfrak{M} ^{1\times d}$ be a tuple of row-norm $<r$ with the property that there exist no non-zero trace-class operators $T_1, \cdots, T_d \in \mathscr{B} (L^2 (\mathfrak{M}, τ))$ obeying $\sum _j [T_j , Ξ_j] =0$. Then the unital homomorphism $\mathscr{O} _d (r) \rightarrow \mathfrak{M}$ defined by the evaluation, $\mathfrak{z} _j \mapsto Ξ_j$, extends to an embedding of the universal skew field of fractions of $\mathscr{O} _d (r)$ into the $*-$algebra of closed operators affiliated to $\mathfrak{M}$.
  In their $L^2-$homology theory of von Neumann algebras, Connes and Shlyakhtenko defined a certain quantity, $0 \leq Δ(Ξ) \leq d$, as the Murray--von Neumann co-dimension of the Hilbert module generated by all $d-$tuples of finite rank operators obeying the above commutator condition with $Ξ\in \mathfrak{M} ^{1\times d}$. As demonstrated by Mai, Speicher and Yin, this $Δ$ measures, in a certain precise sense, the algebraic independence of the components of $Ξ$. Connes--Shlyakhtenko proved that $Δ$ is an upper bound for Voiculescu's non-microstates free entropy dimension, $δ^* (Ξ)$, and remark that it is of interest to determine whether these two quantities are equal. Using non-commutative function theory, we show that this is generally not the case, by constructing a triple of self-adjoint operators, $Ξ= (Ξ_1,Ξ_2,Ξ_3)$, for which this inequality is strict, $δ^*(Ξ) < Δ(Ξ)$.

title: Factor-Assisted Density Estimation: When Ambient Dimension Enables Oracle Rates
abstract: We study density estimation in the high-dimensional factor model, whose fixed-dimensional latent factors have an unknown smooth density. We propose factor-assisted density estimation (FADE), a non-iterative procedure that applies kernel density estimation to spectral estimates of the latent scores. The score proxies are dependent and do not follow the latent density, so standard kernel-density arguments do not apply. A refined rowwise expansion separates error into a conditionally centered Gaussian perturbation and a uniformly controlled remainder. We show that FADE achieves the oracle rate in sufficiently high ambient dimension and prove a minimax lower bound separating ordinary nonparametric difficulty from a Gaussian deconvolution obstruction. Together, the upper and lower bounds establish rate optimality of FADE in specified high-dimensional regimes. We also derive $L^1$ upper and lower bounds for the induced observation density, distinguishing latent-distribution uncertainty from the cost of estimating a growing number of parameters. These results formalize a blessing of ambient dimension: sufficiently many observed coordinates can make a simple spectral reduction statistically lossless even for the nonparametric task of recovering an unobserved low-dimensional density.

title: On the Diophantine equation $X^2+p^m=p_1^{n_1}p_2^{n_2}$
abstract: We consider the Diophantine equation \[ X^2+p^m=p_1^{n_1}p_2^{n_2}, \] where $p,p_1,p_2$ are distinct odd primes. Using factorizations in quadratic fields, sharp bounds for linear forms in two $p$-adic logarithms, elementary methods, and known results on exponential Diophantine equations, we obtain explicit bounds for $m,n_1,n_2$, and consequently the finiteness of the number of solutions for fixed $p,p_1,p_2$.

title: Canonical Kummerian Kernels in 1-Smooth Pro-$p$ Poincaré Duality Groups of Dimension Three
abstract: Let $(G,θ)$ be a finitely generated 1-smooth oriented pro-$p$ group with torsion-free orientation, and suppose that $G$ is a Poincaré duality pro-$p$ group of dimension three. The orientation determines a canonical closed normal subgroup $K_θ(G)$ contained in the Frattini subgroup, and for a Kummerian pair the quotient $G/K_θ(G)$ is the maximal $θ$-abelian quotient. We prove that \[K_θ(G)\text{ finitely generated} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad K_θ(G)=1.\] Thus every non-$θ$-abelian 1-smooth $\textrm{PD}^3$ pro-$p$ group has an infinitely generated canonical kernel, where ``infinitely generated'' means not topologically finitely generated. The proof combines the normal-subgroup theorem for pro-$p$ $\textrm{PD}^3$ groups with the classification of $p$-adic analytic 1-smooth pro-$p$ groups. We also obtain a cohomological description of the canonical extension from the Hochschild--Serre five-term sequence and Poincaré duality. Writing $K=K_θ(G)$, $Q=G/K$, and $V=H^1(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$, we identify $H^1(K,\mathbb{F}_p)^Q$ with the kernel of the map $\bigwedge^2V\to V^*$ induced by the triple cup-product form of $G$. Consequently, whenever $K\neq1$, its first cohomology is infinite-dimensional, whereas its $Q$-invariant subspace is nonzero and finite-dimensional. We obtain exact dimension restrictions in small generator ranks and show that a non-$θ$-abelian group with $2\leq d(G)\leq4$ is not Bloch--Kato. In the finitely generated-kernel case, $G$ is a three-dimensional uniform $θ$-abelian group with exterior mod-$p$ cohomology.

title: Symplectic groupoid multiplication and Poisson integrators
abstract: In this paper, we study the role of local symplectic groupoid multiplication in the construction of approximation methods for Hamiltonian flows on the underlying Poisson manifold. We show it can be used to construct a novel multiplicative type of approximating sequences for the relevant Lagrangian bisection. We describe the corresponding theoretical results, their practical implementation into approximation methods on coordinate charts via generating functions, and illustrative examples.

title: Co-designing a Layered Control Architecture
abstract: Layered control architectures (LCAs) are ubiquitous in complex engineering systems. However, in practice they are largely designed ad hoc and mostly dictated by the experience of the designer. This is because there is currently no systematic and practically applicable theory available to holistically design LCAs. Hence, systematically reasoning about the optimality, stability, and feasibility of the LCA design is not possible. We set a first step toward such a theory by presenting a framework for co-designing a two-layer LCA for a linear time-invariant plant. The resulting co-design problem optimizes over architectural design variables (e.g., reduced order model dimension and sampling ratio between the layers) and tuning-based design variables (e.g., the numerical values of the feedback gain or the matrices of the reduced order model), all subject to constraints that ensure stability, feasibility, and compute properties of the closed-loop LCA. The proposed formulation allows to make informed tradeoffs along the Pareto front traced over different axes of optimality, e.g., speed, accuracy or computational effort. We demonstrate the effect of making various tradeoffs in a simple numerical example.

title: $p$-Laplace Serrin problem on planar annuli
abstract: We prove a rigidity result for the problem $Δ_p u=-2$ defined on a ring-shaped domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$, when homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed and $p\in(1,2)$. This problem admits a natural physical interpretation, as it describes the steady laminar flow of a generalised Newtonian fluid exhibiting shear-thinning behaviour. Our symmetry result is obtained assuming that the set of maximum points, denoted by $Σ$, is a smooth closed curve, and there are no other critical points outside it; moreover, an appropriate asymptotic expansion of the solution near $Σ$ is required. Although our approach is inspired by the comparison strategy of [arXiv:2505.04458], the main ingredients used there are intrinsically linear and have no direct counterparts for the $p$-Laplacian. This requires the introduction of new ideas and techniques.

title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks
abstract: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.

title: A nonstandard fractional Jacobi pseudospectral method for weakly regular right-sided Caputo terminal problems
abstract: Right-sided fractional differential equations arising in terminal value problems present substantial analytical and numerical challenges due to their intrinsic nonlocal structure and the presence of weak algebraic-type singularities near the terminal point. These singular behaviors significantly degrade the performance of classical finite-difference, finite-element, and standard spectral methods, which typically rely on smoothness assumptions that break down in the fractional setting. In this work, we develop a comprehensive fractional pseudospectral framework specifically designed for nonlinear right-sided Caputo terminal value systems. The proposed method employs a versatile family of nonstandard fractional Jacobi basis functions whose endpoint-weighted structure naturally reflects the asymptotic behavior of right-sided fractional operators. This construction enables the accurate approximation of solutions with limited regularity near the terminal point, without requiring smoothing transformations or mesh grading. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the discrete numerical solution and derive rigorous convergence estimates that faithfully capture the inherent singularity structure of the problem. A series of numerical experiments validates the theoretical developments and demonstrates that the proposed approach delivers high-order accuracy and superior resolution of terminal-layer behavior compared with traditional spectral techniques. The resulting framework provides an efficient and reliable computational tool for challenging nonlinear fractional terminal value systems characterized by weak solution regularity.

title: Weighted Fourier capacities and Frostman restriction estimates
abstract: We study a weighted Fourier capacity attached to compact sets, $ c_{p,k}(K)=\inf\left\{\|k\widehat u\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)}:u\in C_0^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d),\ u\geq 1 \text{ on } K\right\},$ where $k$ is a positive tempered weight. The paper develops complementary upper and lower estimates for this quantity. The upper bounds are obtained from Frostman data, Fourier restriction estimates, and Bessel-potential majorants, which together provide admissible smooth majorants of the compact set. The lower bounds follow from a dual testing argument against positive measures supported on $K$, yielding estimates in terms of the weighted $L^{p'}$ size of their Fourier transforms. For sets of positive Lebesgue measure, testing with $χ_K\,\mathrm{d}x$ connects the capacity with the weighted integrability of $\widehat{χ_K}$. A Lebedev-type Sobolev criterion then gives non-triviality ranges governed by the upper Minkowski dimension of $\partial K$ and the growth of the weight. We also record consequences for Ahlfors-David regular sets and positive-measure Cantor-type examples.

title: An exact computer-assisted lower bound for Fisher-information convexity along the two-dimensional heat flow
abstract:
We study the sharp constant in the differential inequality \[
  I(t)I''(t)\geq c\,[I'(t)]^2 \] for Fisher information along the probability-normalized heat flow on $\mathbb R^2$. The unrestricted log-convexity value $c=1$ is false in two dimensions, whereas the known square-root convexity theorem gives the universal value $c=1/2$. We construct an exact, machine-verifiable sum-of-squares certificate proving the stronger universal bound \[
  c\geq \frac{231691}{250000}=0.926764. \] Together with an independent exact Fourier/Gaussian-envelope construction, this gives \[ 0.926764\leq c_*<0.94176665012062, \] where $c_*$ is the sharp constant for positive-time Gaussian convolutions of arbitrary probability measures on $\mathbb R^2$. We formulate the proof in explicit two-dimensional index notation. The lower bound follows from an exact rational polynomial identity involving a strictly positive denominator, a weighted total derivative, and eleven positive rational Gram matrices. All $491$ recorded leading principal minors are strictly positive and the complete polynomial identity has zero residual. No symmetry, log-concavity, finite-variance, or finite-entropy assumption is imposed on the initial measure. The sharp value remains open.

title: Path Covering Spaces of Posets
abstract: In this paper we extend results concerning a kind of covering space for finite posets that bears some analogy to the topological theory of covering spaces. Previous work focused on ranked, locally-finite posets with a unique minimal element. In this previous work the notion of a covering space based on preservation of path weights was defined, and it was shown that, given a poset, there is a unique universal covering space which has an explicit description. Numerous examples of combinatorially significant posets and their universal covers were explored. In this paper we consider finite posets that have a unique minimal element, but that need not be ranked. We give a combinatorial description of these covering spaces, which we call path covers. We then show these covers naturally form a supersolvable lattice and deduce some of its properties. Finally, we investigate an analogue of deck transformations and give some results relating these transformations, poset automorphisms, and the automorphisms of the lattice of path covers.

title: Infinite-variation Lévy processes are either strongly eroded or abrupt
abstract: We prove that every real Lévy process of infinite variation is either abrupt or strongly eroded, resolving the conjectured geometric dichotomy on the smoothness of the convex hull of the graph of a Lévy path [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Probab. Stat. 60(4) (2024), 2352-2381]. We give counterexamples to the stronger point-hitting conjecture of Vigon. As applications, we classify convex-hull smoothness, Lipschitz-minorant contact sets and Burgers shock geometry.

title: Directional Coefficient Inequalities for Strongly Starlike Mappings in Complex Banach Spaces
abstract: We study a class of strongly starlike mappings of order $α$ on the open unit ball of a complex Banach space under a scalar-profile condition. Using a slice reduction along one-dimensional complex subspaces, we prove a coefficient correspondence theorem identifying the directional coefficients with the Taylor coefficients of an associated one-variable strongly starlike function. We further prove a lifting theorem showing that every one-variable strongly starlike function can be realized by a scalar-profile Banach-space mapping. Consequently, the extremal problems for polynomial directional coefficient functionals coincide exactly with their one-variable counterparts. We apply this correspondence to obtain bounds for $|A_2A_3 - A_4|$, $|A_2A_4 - A_3^2|$, and $|A_3 - A_2^2|$, together with the corresponding estimates for $|A_4|$ and $|A_5|$. We also establish a parameterized Fekete--Szegő estimate and a sharp bound for the second Hankel determinant of directional logarithmic coefficients.

title: Cotangent cohomology and higher-order obstructions of matroids
abstract: We show that matroid Stanley-Reisner rings can have essential deformation obstructions of arbitrarily high order over every field, even at corank three. For every $m\ge3$, we construct a connected cosimple matroid with $m$ fine-homogeneous first-order deformation classes whose proper subcollections integrate jointly and whose pairwise primary cup products vanish. These classes define a joint flat family whose $(m-1)$-jet has no lift to order $m$, even without preserving the grading. For the duals of rank-three truncations of $U_{2,m}\oplus U_{2,n}$, $m,n\ge3$, every nonzero homogeneous class modulo the primary cup image is realized as a higher-order obstruction, and this quotient has an explicit module presentation with $m+n-2$ minimal homogeneous generators. The construction is based on a computation of the full multigraded second cotangent cohomology $T^2$ and its primary cup image in terms of flats and parallel classes of the dual matroid. This computation also proves that $T^2$ vanishes precisely when every connected component has corank at most two, equivalently when the matroid has no $U_{1,4}$-minor, settling the conjecture of Constantinescu, Klein, Nguyen, Singh, and Venturello. The same criterion characterizes formal smoothness of the affine deformation functor.

title: Gaps between roots in ballistic deposition on a strip: linear variance, Gaussian limits and a Poisson regime
abstract: Mansour, Rastegar and Roitershtein studied the roots of ballistic deposition on a cyclic strip of $K$ sites, namely the sites that receive a particle at height one, and the number $D_{i,K}$ of pairs of consecutive roots at distance $i+1$. They computed the first two moments of $D_{i,K}$ for $i\le7$. They conjectured that for every $i$ the mean and the variance are exactly linear in $K$, that $D_{i,K}$ satisfies a central limit theorem, and that the standardized vector $(D_{i,K})_{i\ge1}$ converges to a Gaussian process. We prove these conjectures. The key observation is that the roots are exactly the valleys of a uniformly random circular arrangement, so that $D_{i,K}$ counts occurrences of a family of consecutive patterns. We determine sizes from which the moments are exactly linear, which cannot be lowered in any case we checked, and give closed forms for the mean and variance constants and for the limiting covariance. We also prove a Wasserstein bound of order $(\mathbb{E} D_{i,K})^{-1/2}$ that is uniform in $i$, and a local limit theorem. Finally we describe the limit completely when $i$ grows with $K$: it is degenerate, Poisson or Gaussian according as $\mathbb{E} D_{i,K}$ tends to zero, to a positive constant, or to infinity.

title: Holomorphy rings and the Nullstellensatz over large fields
abstract: For an infinite field $K$ and an ideal $I\subseteq K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, let $J(Z_K(I))$ be the ideal of polynomials vanishing on the $K$-rational zero locus of $I$. A Nullstellensatz over $K$ is an algebraic description of this closure operator on ideals. Hilbert's classical theorem provides such a description via the radical of $I$ over any algebraically closed field. In the present article, we introduce a unifying framework for Nullstellensätze over arbitrary rings using the notion of an $A$-radical, for $A$ is a subring of $K(X)$ containing $K[X]$. We show that a single canonical holomorphy ring gives a Nullstellensatz over every infinite field, recovering Hilbert's theorem when $K$ is algebraically closed. In addition, we give a new characterization of large fields (in the sense of Pop) via a particular Nullstellensatz: a perfect field is large exactly when the \emph{rational} holomorphy ring $A_n(K)$--the intersection of all $K$-rational places of residue field exactly $K$--satisfies the corresponding Nullstellensatz. Finally we study the order structure of the class of rings $A$ for which the $A$-radical gives a Nullstellensatz. We show that over non-algebraically closed fields this class has no minimal element, showing there is no optimal Nullstellensatz over such fields.

title: Single generation of transformation group algebras
abstract: We prove that $C(X)\rtimesΓ$ is singly generated whenever $Γ$ is a finitely generated discrete amenable group and its action on the nonempty compact metrizable space $X$ is free, minimal, and has the uniform Rokhlin property and Cuntz comparison of open sets. In particular, every free minimal $\mathbb Z^d$-crossed product with metrizable underlying space is singly generated.

title: Zhang twists for semigroups and groupoids, with applications to Steinberg algebras
abstract:
Zhang twists provide a powerful mechanism for deforming graded algebras, while preserving their graded module categories. We extend this theory by introducing Zhang twists for graded semigroups and graded ample groupoids. We show that the twisting construction preserves a broad class of semigroup structures, and that two graded monoids are twists of each other if and only if their categories of graded sets are pointedly equivalent. We show that Zhang twists are compatible with noncommutative Stone duality: twists on graded-Boolean inverse semigroups are in correspondence with those on the associated graded ample groupoids. Moreover, in the setting of Steinberg algebras we prove that twisting the groupoid gives the same result as twisting the corresponding algebra.
  These results provide a unified framework linking graded semigroups, inverse semigroup duality, ample groupoids, and graded algebras, while extending the scope of Zhang twists to settings arising from symbolic dynamics, graph algebras, and Steinberg algebras.

title: Quadratic fields of values of finite solvable groups
abstract: We show that if $G$ is a finite solvable group such that $E = \mathbb Q(\{χ(g)\, |\, χ\in{\rm Irr}(G),\ g \in G\})$ is an extension of degree 2 over the rationals, then $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{\pm d})$ for a positive integer $d$ all of whose prime divisors lie in $\{2, 3, 5\}$. Moreover, if $G$ has a composition factor of order 7, then either $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{2})$ or $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. This provides a partial answer to a question of G. Navarro.

title: Chemotaxis models with signal-dependent sensitivity and a logistic-type source, III: Bifurcation and spike-like solutions
abstract:
This third paper in a series on a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model studies bifurcation of positive constant equilibria in one space dimension. We consider $$ \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} u_t=Δu-χ_0\nabla\cdot\left(\frac{u^m}{(1+v)^β}\nabla v\right)+au-bu^{1+α}, & x\inΩ,\\ 0=Δv-μv+νu^γ, & x\inΩ,\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial n}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial n}=0, & x\in\partialΩ, \end{array} \right. $$ where $Ω$ is a bounded interval, $α,γ,m,μ,ν>0$, $χ_0\in\mathbb R$, and $a,b,β\ge0$. Building on earlier results on global existence, boundedness, persistence, and stabilization, we take $χ_0$ as the bifurcation parameter and examine the effects of $β$ and the domain size on the bifurcation.
  Center manifold reduction yields a coefficient $β_{n_0}$ at a simple bifurcation mode $n_0$ of a positive constant equilibrium. The pitchfork bifurcation is supercritical if $β_{n_0}>0$ and subcritical if $β_{n_0}<0$. Stronger desensitization raises the sensitivity required for loss of linear stability. Bifurcation may be supercritical for small $β$ but is always subcritical for sufficiently large $β$. Thus, desensitization makes patterns harder to trigger and favors abrupt rather than continuous emergence. The bifurcation mode increases with domain size, allowing more complex spatial patterns.
  Under suitable conditions, we prove unbounded continuation of local bifurcation branches. We also show that large-sensitivity stationary sequences satisfying a peak-gap hypothesis develop spike-like profiles. Numerical continuation and time-evolution experiments illustrate the bifurcating branches and spike-like solutions and suggest unbounded continuation and increasingly sharp stationary profiles.

title: Duality Theory for Sequent Algebras
abstract: Sequent algebras were introduced by D. Vakarelov \cite{VakarelovSequentALg} as a generalization of contact algebras, replacing the binary contact relation with a relation between finite sets of regions and regions. In this paper, we present sequent algebras as Boolean algebras endowed with a finitary closure operator satisfying four conditions. We study the irreducible closed sets of these operators, which coincide with Vakarelov's clans, and use them to develop a topological representation theory for sequent algebras. We introduce the categories of sequent algebras and sequent spaces and establish a dual equivalence between them, as well as a restricted dual equivalence for morphisms preserving the full Boolean structure. We also characterize sequent congruences in terms of positive filters and minimally decreasing closed subsets of the associated sequent spaces. Finally, we show that the category of sequent algebras with sequent homomorphisms is topological over the category of Boolean algebras, obtaining completeness and cocompleteness and a complete lattice structure on the sequent structures over each Boolean algebra.

title: The $(n-1)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with degenerate curvature
abstract: We revisit the $(n-1)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb{R}^n$ proved by the first author in \cite{Be-6} and refine the result in the case when the curvature assumptions contain small parameters. The standard $L^p$ estimate is replaced by a more complex norm/quasi-norm of type $\ell^p L^\frac{2}{n-2}$ which reflects the geometry of wave packet propagation and the degenerate curvature assumptions. The primary motivation for this work stems from a concrete application to the study of the quadratic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$, which is done in a companion paper \cite{BeBoCh}.

title: Third-moment cancellation and predictable representation in finite-state BSDE approximation
abstract: We study finite-state approximations of Brownian-driven Markovian backward stochastic differential equations when the same one-step increment is used both for weak propagation and for martingale representation. For a centered isotropic state-independent increment with vanishing third moment, we prove first-order convergence of the Markov value field, its spatial gradient, and the predictable $Z$-field under suitable smoothness assumptions. The corresponding orthogonal martingale has maximal $L^2$ size $O(h^{1/2})$. We identify its quadratic representation defect and prove a joint functional limit theorem for the state process and the normalized orthogonal martingale, which in particular yields a mixed-normal terminal limit with path-dependent conditional variance. On the trace-free quadratic sector, the representation defect has the sharp universal operator lower bound $d/[2(d+2)]$; equality holds exactly for normalized laws that are weighted spherical 4-designs. In dimension $d\geq 2$, vanishing third moment is incompatible with exact scalar one-step predictable representation for any finite-state centered isotropic increment. Consequently, every such exact-representation law has a nonzero cubic direction, and a smooth Fourier terminal condition converts this direction into a sharp global $h^{1/2}$ weak error. For the centrally symmetric regular-simplex rule we also identify the leading quadratic GKW component, compute the exact first-order asymptotic of the accumulated orthogonal-martingale variance, and recover it from the general functional limit. Thus the same third-order tensor links weak accuracy and predictable representation, yielding an accuracy-representation tradeoff for finite-state BSDE approximations.

title: Optimal Reduced Representatives of Quadratic APN Permutations in Odd Dimension
abstract: The formal derivative of the reduced polynomial representative of a map on a binary finite field depends on the coordinates, although its differential uniformity does not. This matters for lifting permutations to Galois rings: a polynomial over a Galois ring of characteristic a power of two greater than two permutes the ring exactly when its reduction permutes the residue field and the derivative of the reduction has no zero there. We prove that for every odd $n\ge5$, every quadratic almost perfect nonlinear permutation $Q$ of $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ admits invertible binary-linear maps $L$ and $A$ such that the derivative of the reduced representative of $L\circ Q\circ A$ has no zero and each of its nonempty fibres has exactly two elements. The range is exact: this fails for $n=3$, as computed earlier, and for even $n$ there are no such permutations. For $n\ge9$, a linearization and a projectively injective cofactor map reduce the problem to counting binary matrices: more than 5% of the invertible inputs $A$ succeed, more than half for $n\ge15$, without any classification. For $n=5,7$ we use two independent classifications and finite certificates. Consequently every such permutation is linearly equivalent to a counterexample to the reduced critical-point conjecture of Bartoli and Stănică that lifts to permutation polynomials of optimal differential uniformity over every Galois ring with this residue field. For odd $n\ge9$ the existence proof is checked in the Lean 4 proof assistant.

title: When is a better LLM worth paying for? Stochastic Optimization with Switching Mixed-Fidelity Oracles
abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used upstream of decision-making to clean data, detect label errors, and reconstruct missing values. Yet LLM-assisted data curation creates a new operational tradeoff: higher-fidelity models and richer prompts can be substantially more expensive, while the value of this additional fidelity depends on the downstream optimization accuracy. This raises the central question of this work: when should one pay for a better LLM, given a specific downstream task at hand?
  We study this question through stochastic optimization with mixed-fidelity first-order oracles, which can have systematic bias and state-dependent variance. We develop two cost-aware algorithmic frameworks that allow adaptive switching between stochastic oracles. With known bias, the first meta-algorithm applies a restarted, cost-aware policy that adaptively selects oracle fidelity across optimization stages. Its cumulative cost is no larger than that of the best fixed oracle in hindsight and can be substantially smaller. With unknown bias, we develop a budgeted certification scheme that uses occasional trusted-gradient evaluations to certify the optimization progress and eliminate unsuccessful oracle sources, and show an explicit tradeoff between certification cost and delayed detection of biased sources. We provide concrete realizations of these meta-algorithms by applying biased stochastic gradient extrapolation (SGE) and recursive regularization under state-dependent noise as subroutines. Synthetic and LLM-completion experiments illustrate the qualitative switching behavior predicted by the theory: the adaptive policy skips several expensive LLM oracles and substantially reduces cumulative cost relative to fixed high-fidelity alternatives while achieving comparable accuracy.

title: The best Ulam constant of the n-th order linear differential operator with constant coefficients
abstract: Let $X$ be a Banach space over the field $\mathbb{K} \in \{\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}\}$, and let $L:\mathcal{C}^{n}(\mathbb{R},X)\to\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{R},X)$ be the $n$-th order linear differential operator defined by $Ly := y^{(n)} + a_1 y^{(n-1)} + \cdots + a_n y$, where $a_1,\ldots,a_n \in \mathbb{K}$ are fixed scalars and $n$ is a fixed positive integer. It is well known that $L$ is Ulam stable if and only if its characteristic equation has no roots on the imaginary axis. In this paper, we determine the best Ulam constant of $L$ under this condition, for an arbitrary order $n$ and without any restriction on the multiplicities of the roots of the characteristic equation.
