For the upper bounds, we relate the $N$-qubit construction for binary codes used in previous work of the author to the constructions in OpenAI's Chapter 2 for spherical codes and observe that they both involve interlacing spectra. This leads to a variational problem involving measures constructed from these spectra under the Markov-Krein correspondence. This variational problem admits an exact solution and matches the lower bound.

title: Alpha-convex functions in complex Banach spaces
abstract: Let $\mathbb{B}$ be the unit ball in a complex Banach space ${\mathbb X}$. We study biholomorphic mappings $F: \mathbb{B} \to {\mathbb X}$ of the form $F(z) = f(z)z$ for $z \in \mathbb{B}$, where $f: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{C}$ is a holomorphic function satisfying $f(0) = 1$. Our main contributions are as follows: Inclusion Results: We establish inclusion conditions for $\mathcal{M}_α(\mathbb{B})$, class of $α$-convex functions in $\mathbb{B}$ to belong to the classes of starlike mappings or quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ on $\mathbb{B}$ for specified ranges of $α$. Characterization: We prove that $F(z) = \frac{f(l_{u}(z))}{l_{u}(z)}z \in \mathcal{M}_α(\mathbb{B})$ if and only if $f \in \mathcal{M}_α(\mathbb{U})$, where $f \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{U})$, $u \in {\mathbb X}$ with $\|u\| = 1$, and $l_{u} \in T(u)$. Duality: We present a duality relationship between the classes $\mathcal{S}^*(\mathbb{U})$ and $\mathcal{M}_α(\mathbb{B})$ for $α\ge 0$. Hankel Determinant Bounds: We determine sharp upper bounds for the second Hankel determinant of mappings in $\mathcal{M}_α(\mathbb{B})$ when $α\ge 0$. The results established here directly extend the previous results to the broader setting of complex Banach spaces.

title: Rigidity for formally determined point source scattering for an anisotropic acoustic medium
abstract: Consider an acoustic medium, occupying three dimensional space, whose anisotropic sound speed is modeled by a Riemannian metric which is Euclidean outside a compact region $D$. The medium is probed by acoustic waves generated by a finite number (dimension dependent) of point sources outside $D$ and the medium response is measured on the boundary of $D$ for a finite time period. We show that if these measurements agree with that of an Euclidean metric then the metric is Euclidean up to a diffeomorphism. This result is similar to the result in \cite{ORS26a} where they used plane waves instead of point sources. Using point sources instead of plane waves presents new difficulties, dealt with in this article.

title: Strong Lefschetz property of the Kirchhoff algebra of the complete tripartite graph $K_{1,1,n}$
abstract: By Whitney's 2-isomorphism theorem, the cycle matroids of two graphs are isomorphic if and only if one graph can be transformed into the other by finitely many applications of two operations: separation or identification at a cut-vertex, and twisting. The complete tripartite graph whose vertex set is the disjoint union of two singletons and an $n$-element set is invariant, up to isomorphism, under these operations. In this paper we prove that the Macaulay inverse system (the Kirchhoff algebra) determined by the basis generating polynomial of the cycle matroid of such a graph has the strong Lefschetz property over a field of characteristic $0$. The proof reduces the non-degeneracy of the higher Hessians to the ranks of disjointness matrices of families of subsets (the Gottlieb--Wilson theorem) and to the representation theory of the symmetric group in relation to the Johnson scheme.

title: Local modifications in planar hypohamiltonian graphs
abstract:
We prove that for $n \geq 36$ there exists a planar hypohamiltonian graph of order $n$. As a corollary, we prove that for $n \geq 33$ there exists an almost hypohamiltonian planar graph of order $n$. Further, we exhibit over 100 planar hypohamiltonian graphs of order less than 40, including new graphs of orders 36, 37, 38, and 39.
  The proof utilizes three local modifications that alter a graph $G$ by removing a subgraph $H$ and replacing it with $H'$ to form a new graph $G'$: a plus two modification, a plus three modification, and Thomassen's iterable plus four modification. The plus two modification preserves hypohamiltonicity in general, and the plus three modification preserves hypohamiltonicity in our cases of interest. This establishes the main result beginning with Tsai's order 34 examples.
  Further, we conjecture that among planar hypohamiltonian graphs, Tsai's 34 vertex examples are the smallest order. The conjecture is based on previous results, constraints on the degree modulo 3, and experimentation with planar graphs consisting entirely of 4-gons and 5-gons.

title: Functions of bounded variation are not dense in the Strong BD Norm
abstract: We prove that functions of bounded variation are not dense in the space of functions of bounded deformation with respect to the strong BD norm. Using alternating Riesz products and directional slicing, we construct on every nonempty open subset of $\R^n$ ($n\ge2$) a continuous, compactly supported BD function that is at positive distance from BV.

title: Matrix Completion Discriminants
abstract: We introduce the matrix completion discriminant of a graph as the Zariski closure of the set of partial symmetric matrices whose completion fibers fail to meet a rank stratum transversely. A clique-sum formula for the matrix completion discriminant is established for arbitrary graphs, while explicit defining equations for cycles are obtained in terms of iterated resultants. Using these results together with the analysis of $K_4$-minor-free graphs, we prove that for every cycle-completable graph, the discriminant factors into determinant factors from maximal cliques and resultant factors from chordless cycles.

title: Directional delays and singular strong-barrier limits for Fisher--KPP propagation across a semipermeable interface
abstract: We study Fisher--KPP propagation from compactly supported data across a planar semipermeable interface in $N\ge2$ dimensions, with unit diffusion and $f'(0)=1$. For every finite resistance, the receiving front has speed $2$ and logarithmic correction $-(N+2)\log t/2$. Its phase is determined by a positive directional amplitude on the closed receiving hemisphere. This amplitude is jointly continuous in resistance and direction and is Hölder continuous in direction with exponent $1/3$. It also determines a threshold-independent signed arrival-time difference. Under concavity, the amplitude decreases strictly with resistance. As the resistance $β$ tends to infinity, the amplitude is asymptotic to $2(4π)^{-N/2}I_N(θ)(\logβ)/β$ uniformly on each fixed receiving cone bounded away from the equator. Here $I_N$ is a weighted input moment of the closed Neumann donor problem. Although this moment diverges logarithmically near the equator, the equatorial amplitude tends to half the amplitude of the even Neumann donor solution. The strong-resistance and equatorial limits therefore do not commute. The proof combines critical derivative moments, an integrated Robin trace estimate, Cartesian leading-edge limits, and matching through the wave displacement. The phase and asymptotic formulas require only the smooth KPP assumptions, without the additional restriction $f'\le f'(0)$. Concavity is used for strict resistance ordering and the strict bounds on the limiting equatorial delay.

title: On coefficient theorems for starlike and quasi-convex of type B mappings in complex Banach spaces
abstract: In this paper, we study biholomorphic mappings $F: \mathbb{B} \to X$ of the form $F(z) = f(z)z$ for $z \in \mathbb{B}$, where $f: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{C}$ is a holomorphic function satisfying $f(0) = 1$ and $X$ is a complex Banach space with the unit ball $\mathbb{B}$. The main contributions of this paper are threefold. First, we establish a sufficient coefficient condition for a function $F(z)=zf(z)$ to be starlike and quasi-convex of type $B$ in a complex Banach space. Second, we prove that the Bieberbach conjecture holds for these classes of functions. Finally, we analyze the difference of coefficients for such functions in this setting. The results established here directly extend the previous results to the broader setting of complex Banach spaces.

title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of Kähler geometry: the classical Kähler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Ampère energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics.

title: Fourier decay and endpoint estimates for lacunary maximal operators
abstract:
We study endpoint estimates for lacunary maximal operators associated with compactly supported measures. For every $d\geq1$, we construct a compactly supported, absolutely continuous probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$ with polynomial Fourier decay whose associated lacunary maximal operator fails to map $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ boundedly into $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. In particular, it fails to be of weak type $(1,1)$.
  This gives a negative answer to the weak type $(1,1)$ question posed by Seeger and Wright in 2011 and to Open Problems 14 and 15, contributed by Wright at the 2016 Conference in Harmonic Analysis, held at the University of Wisconsin--Madison in honor of Professor Michael Christ.

title: Interior Regularity for Stable Solutions of Semilinear Elliptic Equations with Sign-Changing Nonlinearities
abstract: We investigate interior regularity for stable solutions of the semilinear elliptic equation $-Δu=f(u)$ in an open set $Ω\subseteq \mathbb R^n$, where $f$ is locally Lipschitz and may change sign. We establish sharp interior Hölder estimates for stable classical solutions in every dimension $n\le 9$, thereby fully resolving a question raised by Cabré concerning interior regularity without the nonnegativity assumption on $f$. For $n\le 5$, we also give a short alternative proof of the corresponding Hölder regularity result due to Peng, Zhang, and Zhou. We further establish higher-integrability estimates for the gradient and $L^1$ bounds for the Hessian in all dimensions. For $n\ge 10$, we obtain BMO and Morrey estimates, extending related results previously established for nonnegative nonlinearities. When $f$ is convex, we extend the interior regularity estimates to stable weak solutions through an approximation theorem. As applications, we prove Liouville-type theorems for entire stable solutions of equations with sign-changing nonlinearities across all dimensions.

title: Pantograph Difference Equations: Stability, Multistability, and Chaos
abstract: Pantograph equations are functional differential equations with proportional delay, typically involving terms of the form $x(at)$, where $0<a<1$. These equations have been studied for several decades and have applications in areas ranging from number theory to electrodynamics. In this work, we investigate pantograph difference equations as discrete dynamical maps of the form \[ x_{i+1}=F(x_{i})+G(x_{h(i)}), \qquad i\geq 0, \] where $h(i)\leq i$. In particular, we consider $h(i)=\lfloor ai \rfloor$ and $h(i)=\lfloor ai^α\rfloor$, with $0<a<1$ and $0<α<1$. We distinguish between homogeneous pantograph difference equations, for which $F(x)=0$, and inhomogeneous pantograph difference equations, for which $F(x)\ne 0$. We first analyze linear pantograph difference equations and establish sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability and for nonconvergence to zero. For proportional delays, analytical stability and instability regions are combined with multi-horizon parameter scans to construct regime diagrams in the $(λ,δ)$-plane. We then investigate pantograph versions of the logistic and tent maps. In the homogeneous case, the dynamics evolves through step-like plateaus whose lengths increase at least exponentially, leading to slow convergence and finite-time multistability within computationally accessible time scales. In the inhomogeneous case, numerical experiments show finite-time exponential separation of nearby trajectories, consistent with chaotic dynamics.

title: A priori error estimates for a Hybrid High-Order method on variable-exponent Leray-Lions problems
abstract: We derive a priori error estimates for the Hybrid High-Order (HHO) discretization of variable-exponent Leray--Lions problems introduced in a companion convergence study. HHO methods belong to the family of hybrid nonconforming methods, based on cell and face polynomial unknowns of arbitrary degree. Under additional broken regularity of the exact solution and its flux, we establish a localized error estimate that retains the individual element sizes and a global estimate whose rate distinguishes the purely subquadratic, mixed subquadratic--superquadratic, and purely superquadratic regimes. In the subquadratic range, we also derive a regime-dependent refinement that compares the local approximation scale with the local non-degeneracy scale and recovers the optimal polynomial order when that scale is resolved by the mesh. The analysis relies on variable-exponent approximation properties of polynomial projectors, mean-exponent tools for discrete polynomial spaces, and weighted monotonicity estimates. The framework also covers regularized and mildly non-symmetric anisotropic Carreau--Yasuda-type fluxes. Numerical experiments on Cartesian and Voronoi meshes support the predicted rates and show that the regularity assumption on the flux cannot be dispensed with.

title: On the stability of basis construction in extended Krylov subspace methods
abstract: Extended Krylov subspace methods (EKSMs) are a well known approach for approximating the action of a matrix function on a vector $f(A)\mathbf{b}$, and their block versions are often used for solving Lyapunov and Sylvester matrix equations. EKSMs produce Laurent approximations to the underlying operator, which are generally more accurate per iteration than polynomial KSMs, without requiring a pole selection procedure as rational KSMs do. At the same time, due to the expansion of the search space by not only $A$ but also by its inverse, a number of implementation choices must be made that can affect the stability of the algorithm in floating-point arithmetic. We concentrate on two variants that often appear in the literature and in code, based on whether new basis vectors are built via what we denote as ``mixed channels" or ``split channels." We characterize their loss of orthogonality with an easily computable metric and prove that when $A$ is symmetric positive definite, mixed channels have better orthogonality than split channels; however, numerical experiments demonstrate that straightforward predictions are not possible for indefinite or nonsymmetric matrices. We also provide a modular MATLAB toolbox, \texttt{ektoolbox}, that contains new versions of EKSMs with low-synchronization Gram-Schmidt backbones.

title: Generalized Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv Constants for finite abelian groups of rank three
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with exponent $\exp(G)$. For positive integer $k$, the generalized Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant, denoted by $\mathsf s_{k\exp(G)}(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence of length at least $\ell$ over $G$ has a zero-sum subsequence of length $k\exp(G)$. In this paper, we prove that, for any $n\ge 1$, \[\mathsf s_{3\cdot 2^n}(C_{2^n}^3)=6\cdot 2^n-3 \quad\text{and}\quad \mathsf s_{4\cdot 3^n}(C_{3^n}^3)=7\cdot 3^n-3. \] This completes all the remaining cases in the study of $\mathsf s_{kq}(C_q^3)$, where $q$ is a prime power and $k\ge 3$. As a consequence, for every $k\ge 3$, we have \[ \mathsf s_{kn}(C_n^3)=(k+3)n+O(\frac{n}{\log n}). \] This verifies a conjecture of Kubertin asymptotically. Our approach combines the previous group ring techniques and a recent powerful generalization of the Chevalley-Warning and Ax-Katz theorems introduced by Grynkiewicz

title: On micro-macro derivation of traffic flow models with $(A,B)$-connection and its stability
abstract: We show that $(A,B)$-connections for conservations laws with a flux discontinuity can be obtained as limits of perturbed Follow-the-Leader (FtL) models, and provide continuity and surjectivity of the map associating the perturbation of the dynamics with the flux limiter.

title: A Krause-type recollement for Q-shaped derived categories
abstract: Let k be a commutative noetherian hereditary ring and let Q be a small, Hom-finite, locally bounded k-linear category admitting a Serre functor and satisfying the strong retraction property, with nilpotent pseudo-radical. For every k-algebra A, we construct a recollement of the Q-shaped homo?topy category KQ(A Inj) of objectwise injective Q-shaped modules by its full subcategory Kac Q (A Inj) of exact objects and the Q-shaped derived category DQ(A). The construction uses complete hereditary cotorsion pairs and does not require A to be noetherian. If A is left noetherian, both KQ(A Inj) and Kac Q (A Inj) are compactly generated by special preenvelopes of finitely generat?ed stalk modules. We identify (Kac Q (A Inj))c with the idempotent completion of (KQ(A Inj))c/LI ((DQ(A))c ), where LI is the fully faithful left adjoint of the localization. This paper builds on and generalizes works of Krause and Liu

title: Strong coloring numbers of grids
abstract: For positive integers $n$ and $d$, the $d$-dimensional grid of side length $n$ is the graph $G(n,d)$ with vertex set $[n]^d$, in which two vertices are adjacent if they differ by $1$ in exactly one coordinate and agree in all the other coordinates. We determine, for every fixed $d$, the asymptotic growth in $r$ of the $r$th strong coloring numbers of these grids. More precisely for $n$ large enough, ${\rm scol}_r(G(n,d)) = Ω_d\bigl(r^{d-1}\bigr)$ as $r\to\infty$. This matches an upper bound given by a volume packing argument, which holds more generally for touching graphs of unit balls in $\mathbb R^d$. For the lower bound, we construct in $G(n,d)$ a bramble of order $Ω_d(n^{d-1})$ with each element of radius at most $dn$. This construction was found by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol.

title: Dynamical Conservation Laws in Quantum Spin Systems
abstract: We study dynamical conservation laws and the propagation of thermodynamic structure in translation-invariant lattice quantum spin systems. Using Lieb-Robinson bounds [CMP 28 (1972), 251-257] in arbitrary dimension, and Araki's bounds [CMP 14 (1969), 120-157] in dimension one, we prove conservation of the specific entropy, specific energy, and specific relative entropy under suitable assumptions on the interactions. The transported local Hamiltonians admit surface energies that vanish per unit volume in the van Hove limit, and local observables remain a core for the transported generators at every finite time. Weak Gibbsianity is preserved for sufficiently small times in arbitrary dimension and for all times in dimension one. These results provide the analytical foundation for the structural theory of approach to equilibrium developed in a companion paper, and establish partial results toward the conjectures formulated there.

title: A sharp survival threshold for branching Brownian motion in a self-generated resource environment
abstract: We study branching Brownian motion in a resource environment created by the particles themselves. Particles reproduce at rate $β$ times the resource nearby, resource is consumed at rate $c$ times the number of particles nearby, and each death returns resource mass $m$. Let $θ=βm/c$, which represents the number of births supported by resource from one corpse, assuming perfect efficiency. We prove that the population dies out almost surely if $θ\leq1$, even with perfect recycling $\left(θ=1\right)$. If $θ>1$ and the interaction kernel has finite range and is bounded below at short distances, the population survives with positive probability from every initial state with at least two particles, or with one particle and some resource. The threshold does not depend on the diffusivity, the death rate or the interaction kernel. We prove extinction for $θ\leq 1$ by showing the total mass in the system to be a supermartingale. The proof of survival rests on two estimates: a large colony grows if it consumes its corpses with little waste, and a dense colony recycles corpses efficiently. Together these imply that a large, dense colony grows with exponentially high probability, and a standard doubling and restart argument then yields survival.

title: Approach to Equilibrium in Translation-Invariant Quantum Systems: Structural Results II
abstract:
We continue the development, started in [AHP 25 (2023), 715-749], of a structural theory of approach to equilibrium in translation-invariant quantum spin systems. Dynamical Steady States (DSS) are defined as w*-limit points of the time-averaged evolution of an initial state. We show that if a DSS is an equilibrium state of a sufficiently regular interaction, then the specific energy of this interaction is necessarily a constant of the motion. Two distinct mechanisms lead to this conclusion, one based on dynamical surface energies and the other on conservation of specific relative entropy. We conjecture that these properties hold for a natural class of interactions.
  For a DSS admitting a physical equilibrium description, the associated equilibrium states are characterized by a dynamical Gibbs variational principle: they are precisely the minimizers of the specific relative entropy from the initial state over the physical equilibrium states. The achieved minimum equals the increase of specific entropy.
  The structural theory also yields characterizations of approach to thermal equilibrium, based on two model-dependent questions: restoration of a sufficiently local thermodynamic description at large times and classification of the corresponding local constants of motion. Once locality is restored, the constants of motion determine the possible asymptotic equilibrium states. In particular, if finite-range locality is restored and the energy is the only finite-range constant of the motion, then every DSS is a thermal equilibrium state at the temperature fixed by energy conservation. The finite-time dynamical input underlying this theory is established in a companion paper.

title: Kernel-Based Heterogeneous Mean Field Games on a Continuum Type Space
abstract: This paper studies a class of heterogeneous mean field games on a continuum type space, in which interactions are generated by a Hilbert-Schmidt kernel operator acting on the type-indexed mean state profile. The control set is allowed to be a general closed convex subset of a Euclidean space, and the optimal feedback is characterized through the unique maximizer of the Hamiltonian. For a prescribed mean-field path, the stochastic maximum principle leads to a family of fully coupled forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) indexed by the agent type. Under Lipschitz conditions and a monotonicity assumption on the reduced coefficients, the frozen FBSDE is globally well posed. We then formulate the consistency problem as a fixed-point problem for the kernel mean-field path. When the operator norm of the interaction kernel is sufficiently small, the resulting map has an invariant ball and is continuous and compact, so that Schauder's theorem yields existence of a mean field Nash equilibrium. Uniqueness follows under an aggregate monotonicity condition adapted to the kernel coupling. A linear-quadratic example illustrates how finite-rank interactions and heterogeneous risk preferences produce coupled collective modes, and yields a spectral smallness condition for existence and an explicit sufficient condition for uniqueness.

title: Ordinary lines, point degrees, and matroid density
abstract:
For every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}^d$ with full affine span, we prove that some point lies on at least $n+1-2n/(d+1)$ spanned lines, which is best possible in every dimension. By successive contraction, this implies the sharp bound $r+(\ell-3)\binom r2$ on the number of elements of a simple rank-$r$ complex-representable matroid excluding $U_{2,\ell}$ as a minor, which removes the sufficiently-large-rank assumption from the bound of Geelen, Nelson, and Walsh. An arithmetic application shows that rank-$r$ integer matrices whose maximal minors have absolute value at most $Δ$ have at most $O(Δr^2)$ distinct columns, resolving a question of Averkov and Schymura.
  We prove that a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}^3$ determines at least $n^2/40$ ordinary lines whenever no plane contains more than $2n/3$ of the points. This answers a question of Basit, Dvir, Saraf, and Wolf. We also prove upper bounds on average line length and lower bounds on the number of points incident to many spanned lines in high-dimensional point sets.
  The proofs combine contraction of concentrated flats with normalization of the point vectors and second- and fourth-moment estimates on their pairwise correlations. This approach builds on the design matrix method.

title: Local Tate duality for syntomic cohomology in positive characteristic
abstract: Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p>0$. We show that syntomic cohomology over $k$, with coefficients, and defined using Dodd's theory of $F$-gauges, satisfies local Tate duality. We also prove that syntomic cohomology over the ring of integers of $k$, again with coefficients, is Lagrangian with respect to the duality pairing. Finally, we show that, for $p>2$, these results recover Shatz's duality and Milne's orthogonality results for the cohomology of finite flat group schemes of $p$-power order over $k$.

title: Time Delay of KPP Fronts Across a Semipermeable Barrier
abstract: We study a KPP reaction--diffusion equation on the real line with a semipermeable barrier at the origin, where the flux is continuous and the density jump is proportional to the spatial derivative. With diffusion and linear growth normalized to one, let $β$ denote the barrier resistance. For initial data equal to one sufficiently far to the left and zero near the barrier and on the receiving side, we prove convergence on the receiving side to a minimal-speed wave with a unique phase in the Bramson frame. The difference between distant first-arrival times with and without the barrier therefore has a finite limit $τ_β$, independent of the arrival level and continuous in $β$. For concave KPP reactions, this delay is strictly increasing in $β$ and satisfies $τ_β=Kβ+o(β)$ as $β\downarrow0$, with $K>1/4$. Without the concavity assumption, the strong-barrier expansion is $τ_β=\frac12\logβ-\frac12\log\logβ+C+o(1)$, where $C$ is determined by the homogeneous reference amplitude and the closed donor-side Neumann evolution. The analysis relates the sustained interface input to the front phase through leading-edge estimates, interior matching, and parameter-uniform moment bounds.

title: Modularity criteria for multiple Eisenstein series
abstract: We give two criteria for a linear combination of multiple Eisenstein series of fixed weight to be a modular form, one in terms of its Fourier coefficients and one in terms of its $L$-function. The first criterion follows from an exact transformation formula under $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$, which describes the modular defect of multiple Eisenstein series explicitly. The second criterion is a Hecke converse theorem for multiple Eisenstein series, which shows that the functional equation of the $L$-function alone already implies modularity.

title: A refinement of the strange duality conjecture on K3 surfaces
abstract: Let $v,w$ be primitive Mukai vectors of positive rank on a polarized K3 surface with $χ(v\otimes w)=0$. Marian and Oprea conjectured that the strange duality map $H^0(M(v),Θ_w)^\vee\to H^0(M(w),Θ_v)$ is either zero or an isomorphism. We give three families of counterexamples to this conjecture. In each of them the map is nonzero but fails to be an isomorphism: in the first (a quartic surface) it is not surjective; in the second (Picard rank one, including very general polarized K3 surfaces) the source has strictly larger dimension than the target; and in the third (an elliptic surface) source and target both have dimension six, yet the map has rank five. The three examples share a common mechanism: one of the moduli spaces carries an effective divisor of square $-2$ on which a theta line bundle has negative degree, so that this theta line bundle is not nef and has nonvanishing higher cohomology, and the theta sections produced by the strange duality map vanish to excess order along this divisor. We therefore propose a refined conjecture, in which both theta line bundles are assumed to be big and nef, for instance ample.

title: Local Extrema and Infinite Derivatives of the Delange Function of Base 3
abstract: In the ternary Hamming cube $Q_n^3$, the smallest number $ξ_n(m)$ of edges leaving a set of $m$ vertices is $2(nm-S_3(m))$, where $S_3(m)=\sum_{j<m}s_3(j)$ and $s_3$ is the ternary digit sum. After rescaling, these numbers are the values at the points $m/3^n$ of a continuous function $T$ of Takagi type, the Delange function of base $3$. Both facts are known. In this paper, we study the local structure of $T$. The local minima of $T$ are exactly the ternary rationals, that is, the numbers $m/3^n$ with integers $m$ and $n\ge0$. The local maxima are exactly the points $(m+1/2)/3^n+k$, where $k$, $m$ and $n$ are integers with $n\ge0$, $0\le m<3^n$ and $s_3(m)=n$. We also characterize the points $x$ where $T$ has an infinite derivative from one or both sides, in terms of their ternary digits $ξ_1,ξ_2,\ldots$. At a ternary rational the derivative is $+\infty$ from the right and $-\infty$ from the left. At every other point, the derivative from the right is $+\infty$ exactly when the digit slopes $2\sum_{j\le n}(1-ξ_j)$ tend to $+\infty$. The derivative from the left is $+\infty$ exactly when a stronger condition holds, which also involves the lengths of the maximal strings of consecutive zeros among the digits $ξ_j$. For the value $-\infty$ the two sides are exchanged, and twos replace zeros. In particular, $T$ has an infinite derivative at every rational point that is not a ternary rational and whose period has different numbers of zeros and twos. For the finite cubes, we show that over every block of sizes $a3^k\le m\le(a+1)3^k$, the maximum of $ξ_n(m)$ exceeds the larger of its values at the two ends of the block by exactly $\max\{3^{k-|d|}-1,0\}$, where $d=n-k-s_3(a)$. Finally, the variation $V_n$ of $T$ over the partition of $[0,1]$ into the $3^n$ intervals $[m/3^n,(m+1)/3^n]$ satisfies $V_n/\sqrt n\to4/\sqrt{3π}$, and we compute the Fourier coefficients of $T$.

title: A geometric criterion for the dimension of Morgan-Scott spline spaces $S_{2r}^r(Δ_{\mathrm{MS}})$
abstract: We establish a geometric dimension criterion for spline spaces on nondegenerate standard Morgan-Scott triangulations with four distinct edge directions at each interior vertex. For every integer $r\ge1$, concurrence of the three auxiliary lines joining corresponding interior and boundary vertices implies that $\dim S_{2r}^r(Δ_{\mathrm{MS}})$ exceeds the Schumaker lower bound by one. The proof constructs a quadratic form through the six dual spoke points and uses its $r$th power to define a nonzero functional annihilating the image of the smoothing-cofactor map. Diener's upper bound then gives the dimension formula. We also give a matrix representation of this functional and an explicit example in the quadratic case. Combined with the known necessary conditions and the negative-branch exclusion of Deng, Feng, and Kozak, the result yields a necessary and sufficient concurrence criterion for $r>2$.

title: Greedy multiscale kernel algorithms
abstract: Multiscale kernel approximation and greedy kernel algorithms are two established tools for scattered data approximation. We combine them into greedy multiscale kernel algorithms, in which every level of a multiscale residual correction is constructed by a greedy kernel algorithm. For the multiscale $f$-greedy algorithm we prove convergence rates in the number of selected centres which coincide (up to an arbitrarily small loss in the exponent) with the rates of the single-scale $f$-greedy algorithm. The gain of the multiscale construction is in the stability, and we make this precise by a two-sided estimate for the condition number of kernel matrices with rescaled kernels. The lower bound shows that any single-scale method, and in particular the $f$-greedy algorithm, pays for its convergence rate with condition numbers growing at least like a power of the number of centres. In contrast, the multiscale scaling of the kernel keeps this lower bound fixed on every level without changing the rate. The upper bound identifies the separation of the centres at the scale of the kernel as the quantity to control. We give the operation counts of all the methods considered and compare the greedy multiscale algorithms numerically with single-scale greedy and classical multiscale methods, in terms of error, time and conditioning.

title: Two-element factors and finite bases for additively idempotent semirings
abstract: For every additively idempotent semiring $S$ in the constant-free signature, $S$ is finitely based if and only if $S\times E$ is finitely based when $E=M_2$ or $T_2$. For each $E\in\{L_2,R_2,D_2,N_2\}$, both implications fail in general: we give a finitely based semiring whose product with $E$ is nonfinitely based and a nonfinitely based semiring whose product with $E$ is finitely based.

title: A Hybrid High-Order method for variable-exponent Leray-Lions problems with convergence under minimal regularity
abstract: We consider a homogeneous Dirichlet problem for nonlinear elliptic equations in divergence form with Leray--Lions fluxes of variable growth. The class includes the variable-exponent $p(\cdot)$-Laplacian and regularized Carreau--Yasuda-type laws. We propose and analyze a Hybrid High-Order (HHO) discretization on general polytopal meshes, a hybrid nonconforming method based on cell and face polynomial unknowns of arbitrary degree. We develop a variable-exponent polynomial and discrete functional toolkit centered on a mean-exponent norm equivalence, together with inverse, trace, Poincaré--Wirtinger, Sobolev--Poincaré, discrete Lebesgue embedding, interpolation, and compactness estimates adapted to HHO unknowns. We then establish well-posedness of the nonlinear discrete problem and convergence without assuming additional regularity of the exact solution beyond its natural energy space. The discrete potential converges strongly in every uniformly subcritical variable-exponent Lebesgue space, the reconstructed gradient converges strongly in the natural variable-exponent space, and the stabilization energy vanishes. Numerical experiments in two, three, and four space dimensions confirm convergence for singular solutions and for exponent fields ranging from close to $1$ up to $6$. Quantitative a priori error estimates for the same method are derived in a companion paper.

title: Generic Mean Curvature Flow With Rough Weights
abstract: We prove the generic existence of mean curvature flows in spaces with rough weights. Our weak solutions are both unit-density Brakke flows and distributional solutions. Such a generic statement is optimal in the sense that we consider weights that are too rough to have well-defined traces on every hypersurface.

title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
abstract: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

title: Algorithms for computing basins of attraction associated with a rational self-map of the Hopf fibration based on Lyapunov exponents
abstract:
The objective of this work is twofold. One, we develop a theory of iteration for complex rational functions so that the problems of overflow and indeterminacy caused by null, or almost null, denominators can be avoided when developing implementations. Second, we present easily implementable methods that allow the calculation of attracting cycles as well as the graphical representation of their basins of attraction.
  In order to deal with our first goal, we work with homogeneous complex coordinates, and we take the complex projective line as a model, which is expressed as a quotient of the 3-sphere through the Hopf fibration. An irreducible representation of a rational function can now be presented as a Hopf fibration endomorphism. As well as our second goal is concerned, we use Lyapunov functions and exponents to calculate the cycles associated with endomorphisms and to graphically represent the corresponding basins of attraction. We point out that our algorithms are based on the calculation of a finite set of non-negative real constants, and their calculation does not depend on the previous determination of the fixed points or attracting cycles.

title: Imaginary quadratic fields of class number at most 2000
abstract:
We determine all imaginary quadratic fields with class number at most 2000, unconditionally: there are
  16,453,493 of them, and the largest $|d_K|$ among them is 1,062,350,083. To our knowledge, such a list was
  previously known only for class number at most 100. We make explicit a recent argument, released by OpenAI and
  not refereed, that excludes Landau-Siegel zeros: every real zero $β$ of $L(s,χ)$, for a primitive real
  character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, satisfies $(1-β)\log q\ge5.8\cdot10^{-4}$. An elementary lower bound
  for $L(1,χ)$ then shows that a field with class number at most 2000 has $|d_K|<1.61\cdot10^{15}$. The fields
  with $6\cdot2^{28}\le|d_K|\le1.65\cdot10^{15}$ are excluded by Watkins' sieve, and those below are read from the
  class group tables of Mosunov and Jacobson. As a consequence, the lists of Cremona and Sutherland of imaginary
  quadratic orders with class number at most 1000, and the counts of Holmin, Jones, Kurlberg, McLeman and Petersen
  for odd class numbers up to 1999, previously known under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, hold
  unconditionally. The two steps, the bound for $β$ and the bound for $|d_K|$, are proved in Lean, building on
  the existing formalization of that argument, and the proofs are checked by two independent kernels. The
  contributions of AI systems to this work are stated in the paper.

title: Fixed-spinor radial solutions of a perturbed Euclidean spinorial Yamabe equation
abstract:
We study the perturbed Euclidean spinorial Yamabe equation \[ D_{g_{\mathbb R^n}}ψ
  =
  \frac n2\bigl(1+\varepsilon K(x)\bigr)
  |ψ|^{2^*-2}ψ
  \qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^n,\quad n\ge2, \]where $2^*:=2n/(n-1)$, $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter and $K$ is a prescribed radial function. We establish a finite-dimensional reduction within a radial spinor space determined by a fixed unit spinor, reducing the problem to the analysis of a function of the dilation parameter. Under suitable assumptions on $K$, we obtain explicit existence criteria for solutions with this prescribed spinorial structure, together with a multiplicity criterion yielding solutions associated with distinct scales. These criteria are expressed in terms of the behavior of $K$ at the origin and weighted integral quantities.

title: Semiclassical Band Splitting in the Infinite Chern Band Model
abstract: We study the two lowest Bloch bands of the infinite Chern band model in the semiclassical limit. When the Berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of \(π\), we derive an explicit asymptotic formula for their exponentially small splitting, uniformly over the Brillouin torus. The proof combines Agmon estimates and WKB approximations for a matrix Schrödinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. Geometric properties of the Agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. We provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the Berry curvature parameter.

title: A quantitative Robin Pólya--Szegő theorem for tangential polygons
abstract: We extend the quantitative Dirichlet theorem of Gui, Hu, and Li \cite{GuiHuLi2026} to Robin torsional rigidity. For every fixed $β>0$, we prove that the regular $N$-gon uniquely maximizes Robin torsional rigidity among tangential $N$-gons of prescribed area. Our explicit perimeter deficit bound contains the Dirichlet deficit obtained by Gui, Hu, and Li \cite{GuiHuLi2026} and an additional Robin term that is positive for nonregular tangential polygons. For triangles, we answer the fixed-area optimization problem recorded as open by Keady and Wiwatanapataphee \cite[Appendix A.1.2]{KeadyWiwatanapataphee2016}. We also establish strict monotonicity along equal-area regular polygons as the number of sides increases, with an explicit bound for each consecutive gap. The proof combines mixed Robin--Neumann triangular cells, spectral estimates for angular concavity, and a quantitative scaling estimate.

title: Half-space last passage percolation with inhomogeneous first row
abstract: We consider exponential last passage percolation in half-space with a deterministic first row. This model corresponds to a version of TASEP in half-space in which particles enter at the origin and are restricted by a moving wall. We determine the possible limiting distributions of rescaled last passage times depending on the boundary strength and the choice of the wall. As key inputs to our analysis, we establish several results for point-to-point half-space last passage times, including upper tail bounds, weak convergence, and bounds on the probabilities that geodesics touch the diagonal for certain start and end points.

title: An Eventown Result for Multisets
abstract:
We study an extension of the Eventown problem of sets to multisets on $[n] = \{1,2,...,n\}$. A multiset is called $m$-bounded if each element has multiplicity at most $m$. The intersection of two multisets is defined as the multiset in which each element has multiplicity equal to the minimum of its multiplicities in the two original multisets. A family of $m$-bounded multisets is called an Eventown family if every member and the intersection of every pair of distinct members has even cardinality, with cardinalities counted with multiplicities. We determine the maximum size $E_m(n)$ of such a family for every $m$ and $n$. We show that $
E_{2q}(n)=(q+1)^n, $ and $ E_{2q+1}(n)=(q+1)^{n-2k}\bigl((q+1)^2+1\bigr)^k,$ where $k=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. In particular, the case $m=1$ recovers the classical Eventown theorem for sets. We also characterize all extremal families for $m\ge2$. For even $m$, the unique extremal family consists of all multisets in which every element has even multiplicity. For odd $m\ge3$, every extremal family has a product structure arising from two explicit families on pairs of coordinates, together with an additional coordinate restricted to even multiplicities when $n$ is odd. Consequently, there are exactly $k+1$ extremal types up to permutations of the ground set.

title: Degree Growth of Rational Maps with Laurent Property
abstract:
Algebraic entropy measures the exponential growth of the degrees of iterates of rational self-maps. It is introduced by Bellon and Viallet in \cite{BellonandViallet}. We study degree growth for rational maps arising from recurrences with the Laurent property, with particular emphasis on Gale--Robinson recurrences. We develop a direct method for determining the degree growth from the recurrence relation itself, reducing the problem to the study of associated max-linear, or tropical recurrences.
  We first obtain a closed formula for the degrees of iterates for a broad class of homogeneous quadratic Laurent recurrences. We then apply this result to the two-term Gale--Robinson family and derive an explicit quadratic growth formula with a periodic correction term. For three-term Gale--Robinson recurrences, we express the algebraic entropy in terms of the associated tropical growth rate sequence. Based on explicit computations, we formulate a conjecture for the general three-term family predicting quadratic growth with a periodic correction. We prove the conjecture for the infinite family with parameters $p=1$, $q=2$, and $r\geq3$.

title: Augmentation curve for torus knots
abstract: We prove a version of topological recursion for the correlation differentials of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of torus knots on the corresponding augmentation curves, following the proposal of Gu, Jockers, Klemm, and Soroush. To this end, we explicitly construct the spectral curve from the so-called auxiliary curve of Brini, Eynard, and Mariño and prove that it coincides with the augmentation curve for every torus knot with coprime $(r,s)$. Finally, our version of topological recursion proves the higher-genus closed-string prediction of the Aganagic--Vafa conjecture for all torus knot augmentation curves.

title: Iterative Bounded Distance Decoding With 2-Bit Reliability Marker For Product-Like Codes
abstract: We propose a novel soft-aided hard-decision decoding scheme for product codes based on two-bit quantized reliability markers. In particular, one bit is used for a two-level tolerance miscorrection check to validate the bounded distance decoding (BDD) result, while the other identifies bits to be randomly flipped upon BDD failure and miscorrection. List decoding is incorporated to further facilitate the error performance. Density evolution is performed for the design of the quantization thresholds. Compared to iterative BDD, the proposed scheme requires only moderate increases in memory and computational overhead. Simulation results verify that our scheme outperforms several unquantized soft-aided decoders, while maintaining small memory costs and low BDD attempts.

title: Schwarz $\mathrm{P}$ and Schwarz $\mathrm{D}$ as free-boundary minimal disks in a tetragonal disphenoid: exact areas
abstract: Let $T$ be the tetragonal disphenoid whose four congruent faces are isosceles triangles with sides $2,\sqrt3,\sqrt3$, so that the dihedral angles are $π/2$ along one opposite pair of edges and $π/3$ along the remaining four. By Smyth's theorem $T$ contains three embedded minimal disks meeting $\partial T$ orthogonally; the symmetry group $D_{2d}$ of $T$ fixes one and interchanges the other two. We identify all three completely. The distinguished disk is a patch of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{P}$ surface}$ and the congruent pair are patches of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{D}$ surface}$, with exact areas \[ \operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{A}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} {K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} = 0.781700961348056\ldots, \] \[ \operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{B}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} {2\,K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} = 0.639630785585503\ldots \] in the normalization $\operatorname{Vol}(T)=2/3$, inradius $r_T=\sqrt2/4$. In particular $2\,\operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{A})\operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{B})=1$, which we show is the Bonnet relation for the adjoint pair $(\mathrm{D},\mathrm{P})$. The proof is a reversal of the usual strategy: rather than uniformizing the Gauss map, we identify Smyth's three Plateau contours as the $\textit{tetrahedral four edges}$ and the $\textit{octahedral four edges}$ --- classically solved by $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ respectively --- and then conjugate. Both areas agree with Surface Evolver computations of Ken Brakke to all $15$ reported digits. We also show that all twelve corners of the three disks are midpoints of edges of $T$, each of the six midpoints being used twice, and that $T$ is precisely the alcove of the affine Weyl group $\widetilde{A}_{3}$, confirming a remark of Gandy, Cvijović, et al. (1999).

title: On Stopping Sets and Continuous-Time Decision Trees
abstract: We study stopping sets and continuous-time decision trees (CTDTs) for Poisson point processes. We first give a proof of the spatial Markov property without assuming that the stopping set contains finitely many points or admits a finite approximation. The proof uses the multivariate Mecke formula on the complement of the stopping set. We then prove that every $μ$-continuous CTDT has an explicit exploration representation: between successive discoveries, the explored set grows according to a deterministic rule depending on the points already observed. If $μ$ is diffuse, the points are revealed one by one almost surely; this need not be imposed as a separate assumption. We also allow atoms of $μ$, in which case all points at one location are revealed together. Finally, for diffuse $μ$, we prove that a locally bounded stopping set revealing at most one point is attainable by a $μ$-continuous exploration. More generally, an increasing sequence of locally bounded stopping sets, each revealing at most one additional point, can be attained by a single exploration at successive stopping times.

title: Boundary geometry and concentration points for attractive Bose-Einstein condensates with a ring-shaped potential
abstract: In this paper, we study the ground states of attractive Bose-Einstein condensates in a bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb R^2$ under the ring-shaped trapping potential $$ V(x)=(|x|-1)^2. $$ The boundary geometry of $Ω$ may allow the ring $Γ=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:|x|=1\}$ of global minima for $V(x)$ to meet both the interior and the boundary of $Ω$. As the interaction strength approaches the critical value, we prove that if $Γ\cap Ω\not=\emptyset$, the mass of ground states concentrates at a point $x_0\inΓ\cap Ω$ that has maximal distance from $\partialΩ$. Our method relies on exponential upper and lower bounds for the difference between the bounded domain and whole space minimal energies. The essential lower bound follows from a uniform quadratic-growth estimate near the ground state manifold of the whole space problem, which is established by combining the nondegeneracy of the optimizer for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality with a Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction.

title: The derived category of a generalized complex torus
abstract: For any translation invariant generalized complex structure J on a torus we construct the derived category D(J) generalizing the derived category of coherent sheaves on a complex torus and the affine/convergent Fukaya category of a symplectic torus. The category is defined in terms of a non-commutative curved deformation of the Dolbeault algebra of a complex torus. We show that this category is independent of the chosen deformation path, which we prove using non-commutative Fourier-Mukai duality. We also prove that the action of O(2n,2n; Z) on the space of generalized complex structures leaves the category D(J) invariant. In particular, T-duality acts trivially on D(J). We construct concrete objects associated to affine Lagrangians in the derived category associated to a symplectic torus and show that their spaces of morphisms are given by Floer cohomology. We show that our construction is consistent with the homological mirror symmetry conjecture (including its non-commutative version).

title: Postnikov invariants for rational spaces
abstract: In this paper we construct a theory of Postnikov invariants for (complete) homotopy Lie algebras that is preserved by the integration functor of Robert-Nicoud and Vallette. This result is in the same vein as Berglund's theorem, which relates the homology groups underlying a nilpotent homotopy Lie algebra to the homotopy groups of the associated space. We then deduce an integration functor from filtered Chevalley-Eilenberg homology groups to group cohomology groups.

title: Explicit Ricci-flat metrics on a special Schoen threefold
abstract: We give an explicit convergent representation of the Ricci-flat Kähler metric in a one-parameter family of classes on a fixed special Schoen threefold. The threefold resolves a shifted square-torus quotient with sixteen disjoint elliptic singular curves. Radial Eguchi--Hanson product metrics and fixed flat collars define a positive background with an exact $a^4$ volume defect. Spherical harmonics, tangential Fourier modes, Frobenius recurrences, radial ordered integrals, and the flat quotient heat kernel specify the inverse of the background scalar linearized operator. A boundary transmission series has contraction factor $1/15$. Independent weighted zeroth-order and six-dimensional Schauder estimates give the inverse bound needed for the quadratic and cubic Monge--Ampère terms. The resulting source-degree recursion converges for $0<a\le2^{-2260}$, with explicit coefficient, potential-tail, and relative metric-tail bounds. The representation uses specified kernels, prescribed integrals, and convergent series; its parameter interval is a sufficient quantitative bound on this fixed model.

title: Operator space theory from the maximal viewpoint
abstract: We initiate a theory of ``operator spaces" (in other words subspaces of $C^*$-algebras) with an emphasis on the maximal tensor product. The natural morphisms become the maximally bounded maps instead of the completely bounded ones. With this new looking glass we first examine various issues : lifting and extension properties, local reflexivity, inner derivations, similarity problems.This first part is semi-expository while the second one focuses on the class of von Neumann algebras $M$ such that any completely bounded unital homomorphism on a $C^*$-algebra with values in $M$ is maximally bounded (or equivalently is similar to a $*$-homomorphism via a similarity belonging to $M$). We show that this holds if and only if $M$ is the direct sum of a finite von Neumann algebra and an injective one. This also characterizes the $M$'s such that all completely bounded derivations into $M$ are inner. Our main tool for this is a new characterization of injective von Neumann algebras.

title: Reconstruction of Fano manifolds from the orthogonal to an exceptional vector bundle
abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth complex Fano manifolds of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundles and let $V_X$ and $V_Y$ be exceptional vector bundles on $X$ and $Y$, respectively. We prove that a Fourier--Mukai equivalence $V_X^\perp\simeq V_Y^\perp$ implies $X\simeq Y$.

title: Isaac's Condition (TU) is false
abstract: In 2006 Isaac reduced the simple normality to base $2$ of $\sqrt s$, for $s$ not a perfect square, to a property of dyadic expansions that he called Condition~(TU): the upper frequency of the digit~$1$ in $\sqrtν$, along any subsequence, depends only on the tail of the expansion of $ν$. We show that Condition~(TU) is false, already for the full sequence. We give two proofs. The first is elementary and turns Isaac's own reduction against the condition. The second uses the theorem of Kaufman and Mosquera--Shmerkin on the Fourier decay of smooth images of self-similar measures, and gives counterexamples for almost every point of a Cantor measure. All results are machine-verified in Lean~4; the second proof uses the two cited theorems as hypotheses.

title: Weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}$-object
abstract: $\mathbb{P}$-objects were introduced by Huybrechts and Thomas as a generalization of spherical objects. We classify the weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object in the sense of Krug. For $n=1$, this recovers the classification of weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a spherical object due to Holm, Jorgensen and Yang. We also compute the Koszul-dual model of the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object.

title: A geometry-independent endpoint estimate for the Littlewood--Paley $g$-function generated by the Poisson semigroup
abstract: We prove a weak $(1,1)$ estimate for the full Poisson Littlewood--Paley $g$-function on every complete Riemannian manifold without boundary, with an explicit universal constant approximately equal to $3.33606$. The estimate requires no curvature restriction, volume doubling, heat kernel bound, or stochastic completeness. The proof combines a precise Poisson maximal inequality with a convex entropy identity; local elliptic regularity identifies the extension to arbitrary real $L^1$ data. As an application, we obtain weak $(1,1)$ estimates for certain spectral multipliers represented by Poisson time derivatives with coefficients in $L^2((0,\infty),dt/t)$.

title: Modules and operator rings of Reynolds algebras
abstract: We develop a module theory for weighted Reynolds algebras by constructing an associa?tive ring that records the algebra action and the module operator. The categories of left and right Reynolds modules are equivalent to the corresponding module categories over this ring, and their tensor products agree under these equivalences. We construct free Reynolds modules and give an explicit graded description of the operator ring for idempotent classical Reynolds operators fixing the identity. When the Reynolds operator on the algebra is bijective, modules with bijective module operators correspond to differential modules satisfying an invertibility condition. The operator ring transfers the Hom-tensor adjunction, Morita theory and derived functors to Reynolds modules. Explicit computations over a field show that the identity operator gives an operator ring of global dimension one, whereas the zero operator gives one of infinite global dimension.

title: Inverse Wave Problems on Graphs
abstract: We study inverse wave problems on finite graphs from time-dependent measurements on a prescribed set of vertices. With the graph geometry known, we consider recovery of either the initial signal or the vertex wave speeds when the other is given. Initial-signal recovery is characterized by observability of the associated finite-dimensional system, while a single experiment determines the vertex wave speeds under a zero forcing condition and a natural nonharmonicity assumption. We establish stability estimates for both recovery problems, develop a nonlinear least-squares reconstruction method, and extend the results to positively weighted graphs. Numerical simulations illustrate the reconstruction and examine the effects of observation geometry, time horizon, coefficient localization, and measurement noise on its performance. Our results are motivated both by numerical approaches to continuous inverse wave problems, where spatial discretization leads naturally to graph-based systems, and by applications in which the underlying dynamics are inherently discrete and evolve on networks.

title: A number field extension of Ramanujan's identity and its integral representation via the generalized Riemann $Ξ$-function
abstract: On pages 219--220 of Ramanujan's Lost Notebook appears an intriguing modular transformation whose integral representation is expressed in terms of the Riemann $Ξ$-function. In this paper, we establish a number field analogue of this identity. We also obtain an integral representation for the transformation formula associated with the functional equation of the higher power of the Dedekind zeta function recently studied by the present author and Maji. Interestingly, we recover Hardy's integral representation of the well-known Jacobi theta relation involving the Riemann $Ξ$-function. We further obtain a number-field analogue of the extended Ramanujan--Koshliakov formula established by Dixit.

title: Hydrodynamic limits of finite range exclusion processes
abstract: We consider variants of the simple symmetric exclusion process (SSEP) where particles are 'large'; while in the SSEP, each lattice point is either occupied or not occupied by a single particle, in our model each particle is represented by a fixed shape, and the dynamics is so that shapes cannot overlap. In one dimension, this reduces to a finite range interaction that prevents particles from coming closer to each other than a certain distance. In this case, we prove the existence of the hydrodynamic limit, and identify the relevant macroscopic PDE, which is a porous medium equation. In two dimensions, we have no rigorous results, but instead rely on numerical simulations to approximate the diffusion matrix. Under the assumption that the hydrodynamic limit exists in two dimensions, we derive properties of the diffusion matrix based on the shape of the particles.

title: Fundamentals of Potential theory for a hypoelliptic process
abstract: This article aims at solving open questions related to the well-posedness of Potential theory objects in a hypoelliptic setting. We provide here the expression of the equilibrium measure, capacity and electrostatic energy between smooth open sets $\A$ and $\B$ for the underdamped Langevin process. Additionally, the capacity is shown to be the solution of two variational principles which extend the well-known Dirichlet and Thomson principles in the hypoelliptic setting. Due to the degeneracy of the operator at hand, the results display significant differences with the standard elliptic setting.

title: The linear positive torsor presentation and arithmetic purity of strong approximation
abstract: In this article, we define a notion for varieties called linear positive torsor presentation. For varieties with a linear positive torsor presentation over number fields, we establish the arithmetic purity of strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction off the empty set. As a consequence, we recover arithmetic purity for smooth toric variety with no non-constant global section. Moreover, we classify the chain connected class for rational points on such varieties over any field of characteristic zero.

title: Quotients of Calabi-Yau Generalized Fermat manifolds and Log Enriques varieties
abstract: Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties have attracted a lot of interest in the last years. In this paper we study Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties that are respectively étale and quasi-étale quotients of Calabi-Yau manifolds. We produce several examples by studying quotients of generalized Fermat manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. These are complete intersections of Fermat type manifolds all of the same degree and were described recently by Hidalgo, Hughes and Leyton-Álvarez. We describe all their quotients by a fixed-point-free automorphism. Most of the quotients are Log Enriques varieties or Calabi-Yau varieties with terminal singularities. In one case we get a family of Enriques manifolds which is a subfamily of a family described previously by Boissière, Camere and the third author, which is one of the two so far known families of Enriques manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. This family is obtained as an étale quotient of order two of a Calabi-Yau manifold complete intersection of quadrics, the other family is the Hilbert scheme of $n$ points on an Enriques surface. In the last part of the paper we show that these two families are different by computing their second Betti numbers, which are equal to one and eleven respectively.

title: Moment Propagation for the Vlasov--Poisson System with Gyroscopic Forces, Velocity Diffusion, and Specular Reflection
abstract: This paper studies the three-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with gyroscopic forces and velocity diffusion. For the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^3$ and the specular--Dirichlet problem in bounded domains, we prove the propagation of velocity moments of order $k>2$ for weak solutions with bounded $L^1\cap L^{\infty}$ norms and kinetic energy. The proof applies Serre's compensated integrability to weighted mass--momentum tensors to derive density estimates. A finite iteration alternating moment propagation with improved density integrability then closes the estimates. These estimates provide a simplified approach to moment propagation and yield global continuation of classical solutions.

title: Local definable $(p,q)$-theorem and a refinement
abstract: We prove the definable $(p,q)$-conjecture for NIP formulas in arbitrary first-order theories. We also prove a refinement and apply it to dense pairs.

title: A sharp criterion for well-posedness of semilinear Schrödinger equations on the real line
abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear Schrödinger equations on the real line. We establish a sharp necessary and sufficient condition on the nonlinearity for local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces of regularity greater than five halves. This criterion is formulated in terms of the Mizohata condition and is equivalent to explicit algebraic conditions on the nonlinearity. To prove sufficiency, we combine energy estimates with a gauge transformation adapted to the bounded primitive arising from the Mizohata condition. To prove necessity, we show that the failure of the condition yields a dense set of initial data for which no solution exists on any positive time interval.

title: The space of polarized compactifications of an affine variety
abstract: Let $X$ be a normal affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Through the lens of non-Archimedean geometry, we study the space of polarized compactifications of $X$, consisting of pairs $(\bar X, D)$ where $\bar X$ is a normal projective variety containing $X$ as a dense open subset, and $D$ is an effective ample $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor with support equal to the complement of $X$ in $\bar X$. We identify this space with a natural class of functions--the Fubini--Study functions--on the Berkovich analytification of $X$. Through a Rees correspondence, we also give a bijection with the space of homogeneous $\mathbb{Q}$-valued, finitely generated negative non-Archimedean norms (or filtrations) on the coordinate ring of $X$. Using the above identifications, we equip the space of polarized compactifications, and numerical classes thereof, with natural metrics and identify the metric completions. The latter include a space of continuous plurisubharmonic functions in the sense of Chambert-Loir and Ducros, and a space of birational curve classes as studied by Dang and Favre.

title: The asymptotic Erd{ő}s--Frankl--Füredi cover-free conjecture
abstract: In 1985, Erd{ő}s, Frankl and F{ü}redi conjectured that the threshold $T(r)$ for the existence of an $r$-cover-free family with more members than points satisfies $T(r)=(1+o(1))r^2$. We confirm this conjecture by proving $T(r)\ge r^2+r+2$ for every $r\ge1$.

title: Indiscernible Extraction in Theories with Bounded $k$-splitting
abstract: Hanson introduced the class of theories with bounded $k$-splitting, a higher-arity notion of stability, and proved an indiscernible extraction result for those theories assuming the existence of a $k$-ineffable cardinal. In this article, we show that the conclusion of Hanson's theorem is equivalent to the weaker assertion that there exists a weakly compact cardinal, as well as prove additional indiscernible extraction results for these theories in ZFC. Finally, we show that Hanson's construction of total bounded ultraimaginary Morley sequences in theories with bounded $k$-splitting follows from ZFC.

title: Deep Learning of Topological Equivalence Classes
abstract: We demonstrate an application of deep learning to the problem of identifying whether two generating vectors correspond to topologically equivalent finite group actions on Riemann surfaces, showing how architectures developed for semantic understanding have use for pure mathematical problems. In doing so we discuss how desired algebraic structure influences model design, and explore which structural properties of topological equivalence classes the model has successfully learnt.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Federated Learning for Joint Communication and Computation in XR Systems
abstract: The convergence of communication and computation, empowered by artificial intelligence (AI) enhanced capabilities, emerges as a key enabler for realizing the promising functionalities of the sixth-generation of communication systems (6G). To this end, this paper investigates an AI-native, robust network, where multiple base stations (BSs) simultaneously serve several extended reality (XR) devices. The paper then presents an innovative distributed deep learning-based approach to simultaneously manage the transmit and computing powers, and computation allocation, amidst uncertainties in both channel and computing states information. Under such an interference network scenario, the paper proposes a robust approach for minimizing the worst-case delay across the served XR devices, subject to computation and power constraints. The paper leverages a deep neural network (DNN) that can be trained either centrally or in a federated manner to map estimated channels and computation requirements to optimized resource allocations per BS. During training, uncertainty samples, reflecting both channel and computing estimation errors, are injected after the DNN output to account for such joint uncertainties. Our results validate the enhanced robust delay performance and scalability of joint uncertainty injection as compared to uncertainty-agnostic methods and state-of-the-art benchmarks, with federated learning-based solutions achieving near-centralized performance while enhancing efficiency, privacy, and adaptability.

title: Sharp Hessian integrability for the planar Monge--Ampère equation
abstract:
We determine the optimal local integrability of the Hessian for planar convex Alexandrov solutions satisfying $$
  λ\,dx\leqμ_u\leqλ^{-1}\,dx,
  \qquad 0<λ<1. $$ The distributional Hessian satisfies the sharp endpoint estimate $$
  D^2u\in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{P,\infty},
  \qquad
  P=\frac{1+λ}{1-λ}. $$ This settles the weak estimate proposed by De Philippis and Figalli and identifies the larger optimal exponent $P$. We further construct strictly convex $C^1$ solutions for which the distribution function of the Laplacian is comparable to $T^{-P}$ for all sufficiently large $T$. Hence both the exponent and the weak Lorentz endpoint are optimal: $L^{P,\infty}$ cannot be replaced by $L^{P,b}$ for any finite $b>0$.
  As applications, we obtain sharp estimates in Minty coordinates and optimal quantitative bi-Lipschitz restrictions for gradient maps, including an optimal exceptional-mass bound in quadratic-cost transport.

title: Automorphisms of Free Metabelian Lie Algebras, II
abstract: We show that every automorphism of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ of rank $n\geq 4$ over an arbitrary field $K$ is almost tame; that is, it can be expressed as a product of Chein automorphisms (also called one-row transformations). Moreover, we prove that, for $n\geq 4$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(M_n)$ of all automorphisms of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ over a field $K$ of characteristic not equal to $3$ is generated by its linear automorphisms, together with a single quadratic and a single cubic automorphism. The same result holds for fields of any characteristic if $n\geq 5$.

title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
abstract: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

title: Local Convexity and Planarity Estimates for Mean Curvature Flow
abstract: We establish local convexity and cylindrical pinching estimates for hypersurface mean curvature flow under an intermediate convexity condition and integral bounds on the mean curvature. These estimates hold after a positive waiting time and do not require pointwise upper bounds for the mean curvature on the parabolic boundary. In arbitrary codimension, we also establish local planarity estimates for properly defined flows satisfying a uniform $c_n$-pinching condition, without assuming bounded curvature. As applications, the hypersurface estimates yield convexity and cylindrical pinching for complete, spacetime-proper ancient hypersurface flows with uniform Euclidean area growth, without any bounded-curvature assumption. The planarity estimates imply that every complete, connected, spacetime-proper ancient flow satisfying the uniform $c_n$-pinching condition is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-plane for all time.

title: Cutoff Phenomenon for the Glauber-Misanthrope process in a perturbative regime
abstract:
We investigate the Glauber--Misanthrope process, obtained by superposing a Misanthrope dynamics with finite site capacity and a Glauber dynamics which creates or annihilates particles one at a time at each site. In a perturbative regime around the diffusively scaled partial exclusion process, we prove the cutoff phenomenon and identify the limiting mixing time.
  Our approach relies on the information percolation framework developed by Lubetzky and Sly and extended by Tran, which we adapt to accommodate multiple occupancy per site and account for the two distinct correlation mechanisms generated by the Misanthrope and Glauber dynamics. Our lower bound on the mixing time holds under assumptions more general than those required for the matching upper bound.

title: Tauberian rates and the Baire property of ideals
abstract:
We study Tauberian conditions on the successive differences of real sequences which ensure that: (i) ordinary convergence coincides with ideal convergence; or (ii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal cluster point; or (iii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal limit point.
  First, we prove that an ideal $\mathcal{I}$ has the Baire property if and only if there exists a positive sequence $(r_n)$ tending to zero, with $\sum_n r_n=\infty$, such that $$ |x_{n+1}-x_n|=O(r_n) $$ is a Tauberian condition for any of the three previous statements. Second, for analytic $P$-ideals, we characterize the validity of the Tauberian rate $O(1/n)$ in terms of properties of lower semicontinuous submeasures which represent it.
  Lastly, in the case of statistical limit points, we prove that $o(1/n)$ is a Tauberian condition for the statement (iii), whereas $O(1/n)$ need not suffice: in this sense, $o(1/n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for (iii). On the other hand, for statistical cluster points in (ii), $O(1/n)$ is an optimal one among nonincreasing rates. For every positive null sequence $(r_n)$ with divergent sum, we also construct a summable ideal $\mathcal{I}$ for which $o(r_n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for both statements (ii) and (iii).

title: Cohomogeneity one Hermann actions and backward mean curvature flows
abstract: Principal orbits of cohomogeneity one Hermann actions form a natural class of equifocal hypersurfaces in symmetric spaces of compact type. Based on Kollross's classification of cohomogeneity one actions on irreducible symmetric spaces of compact type, we obtain the time evolution of the squared norm of the shape operator and the mean curvature along the long-time solution of the backward mean curvature flows starting from their principal orbits. These results explicitly describe the authors' previous generalization of the results of Liu-Terng on backward mean curvature flows of isoparametric hypersurfaces to this class of equifocal hypersurfaces.

title: The Calderón operator for time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in closed waveguides
abstract: We consider the time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in a closed, cylindrical waveguide with longitudinal invariant but heterogeneous permittivity and permeability. We consider minimal smoothness assumptions, i.e., the material parameters have to be in $L^\infty$ and the cross section has to be Lipschitz with a possibly non-trivial topology. First, we show that the associated Calderón operator is well-defined and bounded in the natural trace spaces $\mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_Γ;Γ) \to \mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{div}_Γ;Γ)$. Second, we consider interior Maxwell problems obtained from using the Calderón operator and analyze their well-posedness. Furthermore, we report some additional results on the location and group velocities of the waveguide wavenumbers.

title: Finite Time Noncollapsing Kähler-Ricci Flow: Gaussian Type Heat Kernel, Gromov-Hausdorff Limits
abstract:
In this paper, we study heat kernel estimates along the Kähler-Ricci flow with finite time noncollapsing singularities over a compact Kähler manifold. The starting point is the type-II scalar-curvature estimate, which gives the natural parabolic scale $r\lesssim T-t$ near the singular time. By combining the distance distortion and space-time cut-off estimates of Bamler--Zhang with entropy, mean-value inequality, and conjugate heat-kernel estimates, we obtain two-sided Gaussian bounds and gradient bounds that are uniform on this scale. Under the global type-I scalar-curvature estimate, the same estimates hold on every scale.
  We then use these estimates and the monotonicity of the $W_1$-distance between conjugate heat flows to construct a canonical singular-time pseudo-distance. The distances $d_t$ (induced by $ω(t)$) converge uniformly to this pseudo-distance. Its metric quotient is the unique Gromov--Hausdorff limit.
  Finally, we apply Bamler's theory and the recent work of Hallgren--Zhang to obtain the following. Every fixed-base-point type-I blow-up admits a subsequential metric-flow limit whose time slices are singular shrinking Kähler--Ricci soliton spaces with normal complex-analytic and log-terminal structure, unique tangent cones, and a polarized Fano fibration.
