For moving base points, the limiting metric flow, equipped with its limiting conjugate heat flow, is a metric soliton precisely under an entropy-pinching condition.

title: A New Bound for the Gauss Circle Problem
abstract: Let $E(X)=\#\{(a,b)\in\Z^2:a^2+b^2\le X\}-πX$. We prove that $E(X)=O_\varepsilon(X^{209/670+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, uniformly for real $X\ge4$. This breaks the $5/16$ threshold suggested by Huxley as a possible limit of the Bombieri--Iwaniec method at the time. The proof introduces two refinements: a cone distribution estimate that preserves separate fourth- and sixth-power contributions in the double large sieve, and an explicit inversion of Taylor-coefficient constraints that cancels the linear error in a pair-counting argument. These refinements, together with the Robert--Sargos and Watt spacing estimates and the Vinogradov mean value theorem, yield the improvement.

title: A proof of the interlacing conjecture for the singular values of Sylvester-Kac matrices
abstract:
Boros and Rózsa (Linear Algebra Appl. 421 (2007) 407--416) reduced the singular value problem for the odd-order Sylvester--Kac matrix $P\in\mathbb{R}^{(2m+1)\times(2m+1)}$ to those for $Q^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{(m+1)\times m}$ and $S^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times(m+1)}$ via a permutation similarity transformation. They noted that $(Q^{(m)})^{T}Q^{(m)}-S^{(m)}(S^{(m)})^{T}$ is positive definite, and also conjectured that $σ_i(S^{(m)})\geσ_{i+1}(Q^{(m)})$ for $1\le i\le m-1$ and $m\ge2$. In this paper, we prove that these inequalities are strict and establish the strict interlacing relation 
\begin{equation*} σ_1(Q^{(m)})>σ_1(S^{(m)})> \cdots>σ_m(Q^{(m)})> σ_m(S^{(m)})>0 \end{equation*} for all $m\ge1$. Here, $σ_i(\cdot)$ denotes the $i$-th largest singular value of a matrix.

title: Equivariant $K$-theory as a global localization
abstract: We establish a global equivariant refinement of the theorem of Snaith that presents the complex $K$-theory spectrum as a localization of the suspension spectrum of $\mathbb C P^\infty$. We prove that the morphism of ultra-commutative global ring spectra from $Σ^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$ that classifies the tautological $U(1)$-representation exhibits the global $K$-theory spectrum as a specific localization, in both the $\infty$-categories of ultra-commutative ring spectra and of commutative global ring spectra. The classes to be inverted are certain representation-graded $U(n)$-equivariant homotopy classes of $Σ^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$, the pre-Bott classes. We also show that for every compact Lie group $G$, the $G$-equivariant $K$-theory spectrum is a telescopic localization of $Σ^\infty_+ B_G U(1)$ by the pre-Bott classes of all unitary $G$-representations.

title: A logarithmic Brascamp--Lieb variance inequality
abstract: We prove a strengthened Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even log-concave measures whose positive sublevel bodies satisfy the local logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski inequality. The conclusion can be written either by adding a rank-one term to the Hessian of the potential or by adding an explicit nonnegative remainder to the variance. The proof uses sublevel volume variations, a one-dimensional Brascamp--Lieb inequality, and the coarea formula. The derivative of the potential under dilations gives an equality function whenever it is square-integrable. For potentials homogeneous of degree greater than one, we obtain a sharp radial remainder.

title: Automorphisms of triality groups over local rings
abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative local ring with $2,3\in R^\times$, and let $ρ\in\Aut(R)$ satisfy $ρ^3=\id$. We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full triality groups in the adjoint and simply connected forms of type $D_4$. Every automorphism is uniquely determined by an adjoint group element and a ring automorphism preserving the trace $T=\id+ρ+ρ^2$; conversely, every such pair defines an automorphism. A square-zero example shows that trace-preserving coefficient automorphisms need not normalize $\langleρ\rangle$ when $ρ$ is nontrivial on $R$ but trivial on its residue field. We also prove a relative rigidity theorem for homomorphisms from elementary triality groups over arbitrary coefficient rings to local targets with $2$ and $3$ invertible, assuming that an adjoint conjugation makes the parameter-one root images standard modulo the maximal ideal. Conversely, every unital trace-preserving ring homomorphism into such a local coefficient ring induces the corresponding homomorphism of elementary groups.

title: A prime plus a square: A conditional 11/20 upper bound
abstract: Let $E_\square(N)$ count the positive integers at most $N$ that cannot be expressed as a prime plus a nonnegative integer square. Assuming that every nontrivial zero of every primitive Dirichlet $L$-function has real part at most $7/8$, we prove $E_\square(N)\ll_\eps N^{11/20+\eps}$ for every $\eps>0$. The proof combines a conductor-weighted mean-square estimate with a uniform estimate for certain families having a prescribed quadratic component. For these families, the large sieve depends on the varying part of the conductor, while an approximate functional equation controls the fourth moment using the full conductor. A zero-detection argument then absorbs all bands of zeros with real part at least $129/167$. The remaining bands and the minor arcs give the exponent $11/20$. The proof includes even denominators, completion and positivity of the singular series, and removal of proper prime powers.

title: Twisted Artin-Schreier Theory I: $(C_p \rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of local function fields
abstract: Over any field $K$ of characteristic $p$, we parametrize the $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ using pairs of elements $(g,a) \in K\times K^\times$, via a "twisted" variant of Artin-Schreier theory. Focusing on the case of the local function field $K := \mathbb F_q(\!(π)\!)$ over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ of characteristic $p$, we use this parametrization to obtain an exact formula for the count of all $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ with a given discriminant.

title: High-order positivity-preserving well-balanced schemes: combining flux globalization with modified Patankar deferred correction methods
abstract: Positivity-preserving schemes for hyperbolic balance laws are typically built from the Zhang-Shu limiter and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta (SSP-RK) time stepping, at the cost of a restrictive time-step condition. The modified Patankar deferred correction (mPDeC) method removes this restriction, offering high-order accuracy, conservation, and unconditional positivity. However, its solution-dependent Patankar weights make the time update nonlinear, so, unlike with RK methods, preserving (steady and moving) equilibria, i.e., well-balancing (WB), is no longer straightforward. In this paper, we construct high-order, WB, positivity-preserving mPDeC schemes by combining mPDeC with a flux-globalization approach. We demonstrate the idea on the one-dimensional shallow water equations, using a WB A-WENO spatial discretization, and introduce a modified local characteristic decomposition that remains stable in the presence of dry states. Numerical experiments on one-dimensional benchmarks confirm that the method satisfies the desired properties.

title: Orlik-Solomon algebras determine the Tutte polynomials of matroids of rank at most three
abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a simple matroid of rank $r$ on the ground set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ denote its Tutte polynomial, and let $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ denote its Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. We say that $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ determines $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ if, for every simple matroid $\mathcal{N}$, an isomorphism $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})\cong\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{N})$ of $\mathbb{C}$-algebras, without regard to the grading, implies $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)=T_{\mathcal{N}}(x,y)$. Falk conjectured that the Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of every simple matroid of rank three determines its Tutte polynomial. We prove that this holds for every simple matroid of rank at most three, thereby resolving Falk's conjecture.

title: Backward stochastic porous media equation with polynomial growth
abstract: We investigate the well-posedness of a backward stochastic porous media equation whose nonlinear term is a polynomial operator corresponding to the slow diffusion regime. The main challenge stems from the structure of this nonlinear operator, which causes the operator to lose maximal monotonicity and prevents the use of standard weak-strong convergence techniques to identify the limit. Moreover, since the Laplace operator makes it difficult to separate the operators and discuss them individually, we attempt to obtain the of limit by investigating the global properties of the operator.

title: An IMEX multi-level domain-decomposition method for the Boltzmann equation on unstructured meshes
abstract: We introduce a dynamically adaptive multi-level method for the multiscale Boltzmann equation on unstructured meshes, coupling the compressible Euler, Navier-Stokes, and full Boltzmann descriptions within a single asymptotic-preserving IMEX framework. Unlike standard domain-decomposition approaches, where independent solvers exchange data only through interface conditions, the three models form a unified multiregime scheme. They share the same globally stiffly accurate IMEX Runge-Kutta discretization and are synchronized at every internal stage through kinetic-to-fluid moment projections and fluid-to-kinetic lifting. This stage-wise coupling maintains temporal consistency across model interfaces, while the asymptotic-preserving structure ensures compatibility with the fluid limit as the Knudsen number becomes small. The active description is selected in each cell through moment-realizability indicators derived from successive Chapman-Enskog approximations. The hierarchy uses Euler in near-equilibrium regions, Navier-Stokes where first-order nonequilibrium corrections are sufficient, and the full Boltzmann equation where a kinetic description is required. Using Navier-Stokes as the intermediate level avoids evolving a velocity distribution in mildly nonequilibrium regions, which is particularly advantageous on unstructured meshes, where kinetic transport dominates the cost. The spatial discretization combines finite-volume WENO reconstruction on triangular meshes with a conservative fast spectral method for the Boltzmann collision operator. Numerical experiments show that the method closely reproduces the full Boltzmann reference while significantly reducing the computational cost. These results suggest that tightly coupled AP model hierarchies are a viable alternative to interface-based domain decomposition for deterministic kinetic simulations in complex geometries.

title: Short-Boundary Signaling for Asynchronous Grant-Free Control-to-Control Communications
abstract: In asynchronous grant-free access, receivers must detect variable-length transmissions and identify their start and end. Existing decoder-aided receivers use start and tail sequences which are as long as one codeword, causing substantial overhead for short commands. This paper treats the boundary (i.e., start and tail sequences) length as an independent design parameter and proposes a convolutional neural network that detects both boundaries from the received waveform and the decoder soft output. Its waveform input size decreases with the boundary length, while the decoder input keeps the codeword length, so the boundary can be shortened without altering the decoder. Analysis and simulations quantify the resulting tradeoff among payload efficiency, collision exposure, and boundary detection. The results show that the proposed receiver can exploit very short boundaries: in the considered setting, the shortest tested boundary, $L_{\mathrm{b}}=16$, yields the highest effective payload efficiency at all tested loads, whereas a correlation-based benchmark with the same sequences performs best with $L_{\mathrm{b}}=64$ at moderate and high loads.

title: Resolutions of compact balanced spaces
abstract: Let $X$ be a compact reduced balanced complex space of pure dimension $n\geq2$. We prove that every resolution of singularities of $X$ is a balanced manifold; in particular, $X$ belongs to the class $\mathscr{B}$. This removes the additional cohomological assumptions appearing in earlier results of Fu-Meng-Xia. The main new ingredient is the linear independence of the Aeppli classes of the exceptional prime divisors of a projective bimeromorphic morphism onto a normal complex space. This follows from the vanishing of curve degrees for Aeppli-trivial divisors and the relative negativity lemma. For non-normal spaces, strict positivity is used to eliminate divisors mapping onto codimension-one subsets before passing to the normalization. We also recall a classical surface example of Grauert showing that the inclusion of compact balanced spaces in $\mathscr{B}$ is strict.

title: Only their cardinality can prevent groups from being quotients of weakly branch groups
abstract: It is a well-known fact that every proper quotient of a branch group is a virtually abelian group. We record that every group of cardinality at most $2^{\aleph_0}$ is a quotient of a weakly branch group; in fact, there are weakly branch groups that are split extensions with free complements. Furthermore, if a group is generated by $d$ elements, there is a weakly branch group generated by $(d+2)$ elements mapping onto it. As applications of this fact, we resolve a question of Thillaisundaram on the existence of weakly branch but non-branch groups with maximal subgroups of infinite index and, partially, a question of Cox and Thillaisundaram on the existence of weakly branch groups that are not invariably generated.

title: Stability analysis of the steady solution for incompressible lid-driven cavity flow
abstract: Steady solutions at high Reynolds numbers are computed using an iterative method that linearizes the nonlinear convective terms. This linearization reduces the original nonlinear boundary-value problem to a sequence of linear problems, one solved at each iteration, thereby improving the numerical robustness of the algorithm and enabling convergence over a wide range of governing parameters. The stability of steady incompressible fluid flows is studied within the framework of a linear problem for perturbations. The original steady velocity and pressure fields are subjected to small perturbations, after which the equations are linearized with respect to the perturbations. The resulting linear problem allows one to analyze the evolution of small perturbations and to establish whether the steady solutions under consideration are stable with respect to infinitesimal perturbations. In this work, the computational implementation is based on spatial discretization by the finite element method on triangular meshes. The stability of the obtained solutions is analyzed by solving a generalized algebraic eigenvalue problem formed after discretization of the linear problem for perturbations. The presence of eigenvalues with positive real part indicates instability, whereas their absence indicates stability. Calculations were performed on a sequence of refined meshes at various Reynolds numbers for the flow in a square cavity.

title: The $L\log L$-Luxemburg Discrepancy for Nonnegative Weights Suffers from the Curse of Dimensionality
abstract: We study the normalized discrepancy in the Luxemburg norm generated by $Φ(s)=s\log(1+s)$. For arbitrary nonnegative quadrature weights, we prove that the associated information complexity suffers from the curse of dimensionality: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exist constants $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $d_0=d_0(\varepsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that \[N_{Φ,+}(\varepsilon,d)\ge c_{\varepsilon} d^{-1}(1.07735\ldots)^d \qquad \mbox{for all } d\ge d_0. \] The result therefore also applies to equal-weight quasi-Monte Carlo rules.

title: On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points in Stochastic $(L_0, L_1)$-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
abstract: We study the stochastic first-order oracle (SFO) complexity of finding $ε$-stationary points of $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth nonconvex functions. Under bounded-variance noise, existing analyses of normalized and clipped stochastic gradient descent (SGD) establish optimal dependence on $ε$ and $L_0$, but the jointly optimal dependence on $L_0$, $L_1$, and $ε$ remains unclear. We resolve this question for an unbiased SFO whose gradient noise has a $p$th central moment bounded by $σ^p$ for some $σ\geq 0$, where $p\in(1,2]$.Specifically, we establish an SFO lower bound of $Ω\big(\big(σ^{\frac{p}{p-1}}ε^{-\frac{p}{p-1}}+1\big) (L_0 Δε^{-2}+L_1Δε^{-1})\big)$, where $Δ>0$ is the initial optimality gap.This bound identifies an unavoidable contribution proportional to $L_1ε^{-1}Δ$. We also prove that mini-batch (smoothed) normalized SGD can attain a matching upper bound, thereby establishing the optimal SFO complexity.

title: On effective equidistribution for product-type self-affine measures
abstract:
We establish an effective equidistribution theorem on homogeneous spaces for expanding translates of product-type self-affine measures seen on unipotent orbits along any sequence of diagonal elements drifting away from walls. In particular, we do not require the diagonal elements to lie in a fixed proper and closed subcone.
  The main new ingredients in the proof of our equidistribution theorem include an adaptation of the methods in \cite{BHZ25} to the setting of product-type self-affine measures, as well as a weighted effective recurrence theorem for intertwined associated random walks. The latter involves decomposing the random walks according to suitable stopping times and applications of intertwined Benoist-Quint height functions.

title: Sharp Cramér-type moderate deviation bounds for the self-normalized maximum of partial sums
abstract: Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d. random variables with zero mean and variance $σ^2\in(0,\infty)$. In this paper, we establish a sharp Cramér-type moderate deviation for the self-normalized maximum of partial sums under a finite $p$-th absolute moment, $2<p\le3$. In particular, we show that $\mathbb{P}(M_n\ge xV_n)=2(1-Φ(x))\{1+O(1)β_{n,p}(1+x)^p\}$ for $0\le x\leβ_{n,p}^{-1/p}$, where $M_n=\max_{1\le k\le n}\sum_{j=1}^kX_j$, $V_n=(\sum_{j=1}^nX_j^2)^{1/2}$, $β_{n,p}=\mathbb{E}|X_1|^p/(n^{(p-2)/2}σ^p)$, and $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. This proves a conjecture of Shao2010. More precisely, we bound the relative error by the same truncated-moment quantity as for self-normalized sums. The proof compares the maximum with the absolute sum while preserving their common denominator, through a reflected-walk representation and Fourier estimates with distribution-adapted smoothing.

title: On the Sampling of Certain Dirichlet and Prime Sums at Gram Points and their Viscosity
abstract: Consider the Dirichlet polynomial and its prime-indexed sub-sum \[ \begin{array}{ccc} E(t) := \sum_{k\le \left[ \sqrt{ \frac{t}{2π} } \right]} \frac{e^{it\log k}}{\sqrt{k}}, & ; & E_1(t) := \sum_{\substack{p\le \left[ \sqrt{\frac{t}{2π}} \right]\\ p\ {\rm prime}}} \frac{e^{it\log p}}{\sqrt p}. \end{array} \] In this work we investigate the statistical and arithmetic properties of the sets \[ \mathcal{C}_N := \left\{ E(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \qquad \mathcal{P}_N := \left\{ E_1(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \] obtained by sampling these sums at the Gram points \(g_n\) of the Hardy \(Z\)-function. We refer to \(\mathcal{C}_N\) and \(\mathcal{P}_N\) as the full and prime \(N\)-th Gram clouds, respectively. The motivation is that the approximate functional equation expresses both \(Z(g_n)\) and \(Z'(g_n)\) through different projections of the same oscillatory phase configuration, suggesting that the geometry of these sampled sums may retain information about the local behavior of nearby zeros. Numerically, we find that Gram-point sampling produces highly non-generic geometric structures: good and isolated bad Gram points occupy markedly different regions of the clouds, the prime cloud of isolated bad points splits into two anisotropic lobes, and the position along the principal direction of the folded prime cloud is strongly correlated with the viscosity of the Hardy $Z$-function \( μ(g_n)=\left|\frac{Z'(g_n)}{Z(g_n)}\right|, \) with smallest-viscosity points concentrating near distinguished extremal regions of the lobes.

title: Uniformization of Julia sets of geometrically finite rational maps
abstract: A Schottky set is the complement of a collection of disjoint open disks in the Riemann sphere. We completely characterize geometrically finite rational maps whose Julia sets are quasiconformally equivalent to Schottky sets. We also prove that the closure of the basin of infinity of a geometrically finite unicritical polynomial is quasiconformally equivalent to a Schottky set if and only if either there exists an attracting cycle and all bounded Fatou components have disjoint closures or there exists a parabolic cycle of multiplicity three. An ingredient of the proof is a new dynamical characterization of pairs of arbitrary quasicircles that are quasiconformally equivalent to pairs of tangent circles.

title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
abstract: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $Γ$ satisfies $\exp(Γ) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.

title: A variation on local trilinear form
abstract: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field and $M$ the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2^3(F)$ consisting of triples with equal determinants. For each unitary principal series $L$-packet of $M$ whose central character is trivial on the diagonal $F^\times$, we determine its unique member distinguished by the diagonal $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$.

title: Scalar curvature, volume, and Weil-Petersson translation length
abstract: We construct metrics on pseudoAnosov mapping tori that make every fiber an intrinsically hyperbolic stable minimal surface, and which have scalar curvature identically -6. Using this, we give a new proof (with improved constant) of an inequality bounding the hyperbolic volume of a pseudoAnosov mapping torus by the Weil-Petersson translation length (and consequently, the entropy) of its monodromy.

title: Singular Yamabe metrics on complements of closed sets
abstract: Let $n\geq3$ and let $Λ\subset \mathbb S^n$ be closed, contain at least two points, and satisfy $\dim_{\mathrm H}Λ<(n-2)/2$. We prove that there exists a complete metric of scalar curvature $n(n-1)$ on $\mathbb S ^n\setminusΛ$, conformal to the round metric.

title: Recovery of coefficients in a Schrödinger system with nonlinear coupling
abstract: We consider the inverse problem of recovering time-dependent coefficients in a system of Schrödinger equations with coupled nonlinear terms. We first address the well-posedness of the system for small boundary data and trivial initial data. Then, we show that the linearized Neumann data stably determines the nonlinear coefficients provided that, at any given time, they are known in some neighborhood of the boundary. The proof relies on linearization and complex geometric optics (CGO) solutions for the linear Schrödinger equation. We conclude by outlining an approach based on the direct use of Carleman estimates to recover time-independent coefficients in the setting of trivial boundary data but nontrivial initial data.

title: Volterra operators on the BMOA space of Dirichlet series
abstract: In this paper, we completely characterize the boundedness and compactness of Volterra operators on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\), the BMOA space of Dirichlet series, and estimate their essential and weak essential norms. We further prove that compactness, weak compactness, and complete continuity are equivalent for these operators. In particular, every Dirichlet polynomial symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\). We also prove that every such symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on the Bergman space of Dirichlet series \(\mathcal A_μ^1\) for every admissible measure \(μ\), extending the corresponding compactness theorem, previously established for \(1<p<\infty\), to the endpoint \(p=1\).

title: On Minimum Divergence for Distribution Reconstruction
abstract: We study the possibility of generalizing maximum-entropy reconstruction, which approximately recovers a probability distribution from finitely many (generalized) moments by minimizing the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence to a reference measure. The reconstruction lies in an exponential family and is also the best KL approximation of the unknown distribution within that family: moment matching and information projection coincide. Replacing KL by a smooth f-divergence, the reconstruction still exists in an associated family, but the best approximation property does not. Specifically, a family is called entropy-adapted if the projection of any distribution matches its moments. We show that, up to equivalence, KL is the only $C^2$ f-divergence that is entropy-adapted, whatever the choice of the generalized moments. We illustrate the consequences of this failure numerically.

title: Edge ideals of gapfree graphs with matching number $3$
abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a gapfree graph with matching number $3$, then every power $I(G)^q$, $q\geq2$, of its edge ideal has linear quotients, and hence a linear resolution. Our approach combines graph reductions based on clique domination of gapfree graphs and matching number with operations preserving linear quotients. We reduce the problem to $26$ non-co-chordal graphs on at most seven vertices. A new preservation theorem for gapfree edge addition, together with known results on duplication and gapfree expansion, handles all but one of these graphs. For the remaining graph on seven vertices, we construct a linear quotients ordering for the square and extend it recursively to every higher power.

title: Localisation of the monkey walk with an "impurity" at the origin
abstract:
The monkey walk is a model of reinforced random walk introduced by Boyer and Solis-Salas as a model for the exploratory behaviour of capuchin monkeys. At each step of the walk, the walker flips a biased coin to determine whether to take a simple, symmetric random walk step on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ or to "relocate", i.e. choose a time uniformly at random in its past and jump to where it was at that time. More recently, Boyer, Falcón-Cortés, Giuggioli and Majumdar looked at a modification of the model, where the probability to relocate is $ξ_0$ when the walker sits at the origin and $ξ>ξ_0$ anywhere else.
  We prove that, for all $ξ_0\in (0,1)$, if $ξ$ is sufficiently close to 1, then the monkey walk "localises", i.e. the position of the walker at time $n$, $W_n$, converges in distribution without any renormalisation. (We in fact prove convergence of the occupation measure of the walker.) This is in contrast with the case when $ξ= ξ_0$, for which it is known that $W_n/\sqrt{\log n}$ converges in distribution to a standard Gaussian (we say that the walk "diffuses").
  Our proof relies on seeing the monkey walk as an infinitely-many colour Pólya urn (a.k.a. measure-valued Pólya process - MVPP) and then prove convergence of this urn, which is not straightforward as theorems from the literature on MVPPs do not apply directly.

title: On the uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the Motsch-Tadmor model
abstract: We consider the Motsch-Tadmor model, a modification of the Cucker-Smale model for flocking dynamics that incorporates asymmetric communication weights. In the case of uniformly positive interactions, we consider the validity problem for the limiting kinetic equation, proving a uniform-in-time propagation of chaos result in the moving frame given by the consensus velocities. The result is obtained by studying the reversibility of the communication weights and by implicitly characterizing the asymptotic consensus.

title: Legitimate Reconstruction Advantage in Wiretapped Semantics-Aware Remote Monitoring
abstract: This paper investigates joint accuracy and security in semantics-aware remote monitoring, where source updates intended for a legitimate receiver may also be intercepted by an eavesdropper. We define legitimate reconstruction advantage (LRA) as the joint event that the intended receiver correctly reconstructs the current source state using received updates while the eavesdropper reconstructs it incorrectly. Source evolution changes the relevance of received updates at the two receivers, so their marginal reconstruction accuracies do not, in general, determine the probability of this joint event. Under randomized stationary (RS) transmission and zero-order-hold reconstruction at both receivers, we derive an explicit joint stationary distribution and closed-form expressions for LRA probability and persistence for general finite-state ergodic Markov sources. For two-state and uniform-transition sources, we obtain algebraic expressions that enable low-complexity optimization of RS policies. Analytical and numerical results show that maximizing the probability of legitimate advantage need not maximize its persistence. For two-state sources, rare-transmission analysis reveals that, at a fixed sum of transition probabilities, greater transition asymmetry can increase persistence while reducing LRA probability. Moreover, optimizing marginal accuracy and security metrics can select policies that are suboptimal for LRA. Counterintuitively, more frequent transmission or improved legitimate-channel reliability can increase legitimate reconstruction accuracy while reducing LRA probability. Finally, a geofencing application translates prescribed LRA requirements into spatial constraints on eavesdropper locations.

title: Causal Sobolev spaces and gradient flows
abstract: We develop a relaxation-based approach to Sobolev functions and Cheeger energies on metric spacetimes, in analogy with the construction used in positive signature. For an exponent $p<0$, we introduce a pre-$p$-Cheeger energy built from a local steepness constant on causal functions, and define the $p$-Cheeger energy as its relaxation in $L^0$; this yields, by construction, a convex and lower semicontinuous functional together with an associated maximal relaxed subslope. We establish natural calculus rules for the resulting Sobolev class. We then define the $p$-heat flow as the gradient flow of the $p$-Cheeger energy in $L^2$ and its generator, the $p$-d'Alembertian. Combining a Kuwada-type lemma with entropy growth estimates along the flow, we show that our notion of Sobolev class and relaxed subslope coincides with the Sobolev class and weak subslope introduced by Beran et al.

title: Model-Driven Deep Learning for Distributed Detection with Low-Bit Quantization
abstract: Distributed detection plays a fundamental role in communication-efficient collaborative inference over large-scale networks, where spatially distributed nodes must cooperate using severely quantized messages due to bandwidth constraints. While low-bit quantization is essential for reducing communication overhead, it can significantly degrade detection performance, particularly when prior knowledge of observation noise is unavailable. To address this challenge, we propose a model-driven deep learning framework for distributed detection with low-bit quantization. For fixed local quantizers, we first derive the exact finite-sensor maximum a posteriori (MAP) detection error and prove that, under conditionally independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) observations, independent local randomizations, and a common quantization-level constraint, identical quantizers preserve the supremum of the average network Chernoff information. Guided by these results, we develop a binary probabilistic quantizer with a trainable neural probability controller and design a tree-structured probabilistic quantizer for scalable multi-bit quantization. The exact finite-sensor MAP error provides the training objective for the binary quantizer, while we derive a computationally tractable Bhattacharyya surrogate objective for training the multi-bit quantizer. For both cases, we derive analytical MAP fusion rules based on the class-conditional probability mass functions (PMFs) of the quantized messages. When the observation statistics are unknown, these PMFs are estimated from held-out labeled data, yielding plug-in MAP detectors. Simulation results show that the proposed method approaches centralized-oracle performance at higher quantization resolutions and remains effective under changes in network size and test-time signal amplitude.

title: A multi-point maximum principle to prove the global Harnack inequality for the doubly nonlinear heat equation
abstract: This work aims to present a new proof of the global pointwise Harnack inequality satisfied by positive viscosity solutions of the doubly nonlinear heat equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Our approach is based on a multi-point maximum principle argument introduced by the authors in a recent article [Calc. Var., 2026]. Required for the proof is a new variation of the maximum principle for semicontinuous functions, which is a standard tool in the analysis of viscosity solutions. In particular, our techniques provide a new proof of the Harnack inequalities satisfied by positive solutions of the porous medium equation and the $p$-heat equation, which were derived by Auchmuty and Bao [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 1994] using results of Aronson and Bénilan [C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris, 1979] and Esteban and Vázquez [Arch. Rational Mech. Anal., 1988]. The results contained in this article have also been discussed in the third author's doctoral thesis.

title: Bézout bounds and rational points on quasianalytic graphs
abstract: For functions $f : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ in quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes $\mathcal C_M$, we establish explicit bounds for the number of intersection points of the graph $Γ(f)$ with algebraic curves of degree at most $d$. The bounds are given in terms of the Bang degree determined by the weight sequence $M$, the degree $d$, and the norming constant of $Γ(f)$ with respect to the space of real bivariate polynomials of degree at most $d$. We give instances, where the bounds are at most polynomial in $d$ and, consequently, the graph $Γ(f)$ contains few rational points: the number of rational points of height at most $H$ is bounded by a polynomial in $\log H$.

title: Projection-Based Parareal for Nonlinear Initial-Value Problems
abstract: Parareal is a parallel-in-time method for initial-value problems that has found extensive applications and given rise to many variants. Krylov-enhanced parareal is a variant of parareal that uses projection techniques to accelerate convergence substantially for linear problems. In this paper, we study a projection-based parareal algorithm for nonlinear initial-value problems with a modified iteration scheme and an arbitrary orthogonal projection. For a general nonlinear problem, we prove a convergence estimate for each iteration step on a fixed time grid. We analyze the errors of the modified scheme and the scheme of Krylov-enhanced parareal relative to the old error as the coarse grid is refined. For a coarse solver of order $p$ and step size $h$, we prove error bounds of $O(h^{p+1})$ for the modified scheme and $O(h)$ for that of Krylov-enhanced parareal at the first potentially inexact time point under mild assumptions. Numerical experiments on two nonlinear problems are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

title: An Adaptive Cubic Regularisation Algorithm Based on Interior-Point Methods for Optimization with General Inequality Constraints
abstract: Nonlinear constrained optimization has a wide range of practical applications. The interior-point method is considered to be one of the most powerful algorithms for solving nonlinear inequality constrained optimization. In this paper, we consider optimization with general inequality constraints and propose an Adaptive Regularisation algorithm using Cubics Based on Interior-Point methods (ARCBIP). For solving the barrier problem, we construct ARC subproblem with linearized constraints and the well-known fraction to the boundary rule that prevents slack variables from approaching their lower bounds prematurely. We employ a composite-step approach and reduced Hessian methods to deal with linearized constraints, where the trial step is decomposed into a normal step and a tangential step. They are obtained by solving two ARC subproblems approximately with the fraction to the boundary rule. Requirements on normal steps and tangential steps are given to ensure global convergence. To determine whether the trial step is accepted, we use exact penalty function as the merit function in ARC framework. The updating of the barrier parameter is implemented by adaptive strategies. Global convergence is analyzed under mild assumptions. Preliminary numerical experiments and some comparison results are reported.

title: A Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Time-Modulated Drude--Lorentz Media
abstract: We formulate and analyze a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method for Maxwell's equations coupled to four time-modulated Drude--Lorentz models: modulated in-coupling, modulated polarization density, modulated current density, and modulated effective mass. The use of electric displacement and model-dependent continuous material states gives a common treatment of temporal interfaces while preserving the distinct physical transmission rules. We derive energy and stability estimates, establish spatial and event-aligned time-error bounds, and separate time-integration error from error caused by misplaced switching times. Numerical experiments in three dimensions and in reduced modal systems confirm the predicted spatial, temporal, and switch-timing behavior, including the field-jump effect specific to the polarization-density model.

title: Mixing time of the lazy and simple random walk on a randomly twisted hypercube
abstract: We consider a randomly twisted hypercube on $N$ vertices and study a simple or lazy random walk on this graph. We show that for both walks the mixing time is of order $\log N$, and the model does not exhibit cutoff. We also establish that both walks have cover time of order $N\log N$, and we show that the chromatic number of the graph diverges.

title: Discrete Temporal CSPs et al
abstract:
We revisit the complexity classification of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) for first-order reducts of $(\mathbb{Z},<)$, established by Bodirsky, Martin, and Mottet in 2018. Following their approach, we give a self-contained proof of this classification, correcting several errors in the argument. We further show that, with the exception of cases arising from finite-domain CSPs, all tractable cases are solved by a well-known uniform algorithm, eliminating the need for the collection of ad-hoc algorithms used in the original paper.
  A central component of the proof allows the analysis to be restricted to first-order reducts of $(\mathbb{Z},<)$ that contain the successor relation. We substantially simplify this reduction and generalize the underlying construction. This generalization allows us to apply the same technique to first-order reducts of the triangular lattice graph and of infinite regular trees, yielding a complete complexity classification for these classes of structures, in particular a $\mathsf{P}$ versus $\mathsf{NP}$-complete dichotomy.

title: Mod 3 Congruence Families for twisted signatures of string manifolds in dimensions up to twenty-eight
abstract: In the paper, we establish congruences for twisted Dirac indices and signatures on closed string manifolds by specializing the two-parameter modular forms of Liu and Wang to the tangent bundle. Fourier coefficient comparisons yield uniform congruences modulo $3$ in dimensions $4k$, $1\leq k\leq7$. Suitable parameter choices give explicit formulas involving only genuine twisting bundles in dimensions $8,12,16,20,24,$ and $28$, and recover the comparisons of Chen and Han in dimension $24$. The level-one Witten genus further strengthens selected Dirac congruences to moduli $729,27,27,$ and $9$ in dimensions $16,20,24,$ and $28$, respectively. The proofs use Fourier expansions in reduced $K$-theory and integer identities obtained by clearing powers of two from the denominators before reduction modulo $3$. We also construct non-string spin counterexamples in each of the six listed dimensions and identify the additional coefficient that obstructs extending the uniform argument to dimension $32$ without further information.

title: Defense Filters for Robust Learning of Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
abstract: Robust estimation of unknown system dynamics from partial observations under attack is a core challenge in learning for control, increasingly critical in multi-agent networks subject to adversarial data poisoning. Existing methods either require highly restrictive assumptions on the adversary or yield weak error bounds. In this paper, we consider identifying partially observed linear dynamical systems subject to adversarial attacks with an attack probability $p < 0.5$ at each time. We propose a defense-filtering framework in which a system designer leverages knowledge of the observation matrix to construct a defense filter satisfying full column rank and subspace separability conditions, which enables the evaluation of a single-attack scenario against observed data. Using this framework, we analyze the constrained $\ell_2$-norm estimator and establish finite-sample error bounds for recovering the Markov parameter matrix $G^*$. This is the first approach to provide provable system identification guarantees via a defense filter for partially observed systems subject to harsh attack environments where the attack probability approaches $0.5$.

title: Gromov-Hausdorff Convergence of Constant Scalar Curvature Kähler Metrics near the Canonical Class
abstract: Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-ample canonical bundle. For any Kähler class $[ω]$, Jian--Shi--Song proved that there exists a unique cscK metric in the class $2πc_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[ω]$ when $\varepsilon \in (0,\varepsilon_0]$, using the properness criterion of Chen--Cheng. We prove that the cscK metrics in $2πc_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[ω]$ converge, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology to the metric completion of the twisted Kähler-Einstein metric on the canonical model of $X$ as conjectured by Jian--Shi--Song. Based on the technique developed in this paper, we can also give a new proof the theorem of Lee--Tosatti--Zhang on the Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of the normalized Kähler--Ricci flow on $X$.

title: An introduction to algebraic groups
abstract: We review the theory of abelian varieties and, more generally, algebraic groups, with a view toward arithmetic applications. We discuss their models over the rings of integers of number fields, their reductions modulo primes, their torsion points (together with their natural Galois action), and the interplay of these notions through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius.

title: GPU Parallel Pareto Local Search for Multi-objective QUBO
abstract: We revisit Pareto Local Search (PLS) for multi-objective quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems. Multi-objective QUBO formulations have gained increasing attention as a universal modeling method and natural input for quantum optimization. While exact methods exist, their unconstrained binary structure makes them well-suited for heuristics such as PLS. At the same time, GPUs offer a powerful classical alternative to quantum-inspired optimization. We develop an efficient GPU-based parallel implementation of PLS for multi-objective QUBO problems. Our approach combines coarse-grained and fine-grained parallelization. On the coarse-grained level, an initial set of supported solutions is generated using weighted-sum optimization, from which multiple PLS processes are started in parallel. At the fine-grained level, neighborhood exploration is parallelized on the GPU by simultaneously evaluating binary-flip candidate solutions across all objectives. Non-dominated solutions are maintained using an ND-Tree data structure to support efficient Pareto updates. The implementation combines several known PLS techniques within a unified CPU/GPU hybrid architecture. We describe the algorithmic components, the GPU-specific design decisions, and report results from a computational study evaluating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Lipschitz-free spaces over separable Banach spaces and their complementability in the bidual
abstract: We prove that the Lipschitz-free space over a separable Banach space is complemented in its bidual if and only if the underlying Banach space is isomorphic to a Hilbert space. This answers negatively a long-standing question of Godefroy, Lancien, and Zizler concerning the case of $\ell_1$. We also characterize the existence of a projection of norm one and extend both characterizations to nonempty open convex subsets. Our approach yields several further results which we believe may be useful for understanding the structure of Lipschitz-free spaces over Banach spaces. These include an isometric representation of such spaces as quotients of Bochner $L^1$ spaces constructed using Gaussian measures.

title: Finite Cumulant Towers for Small-System-Noise Expansions in Nonlinear Filtering
abstract: We study asymptotic expansions for nonlinear filtering in the small-system-noise regime. Our main result is that the expansion coefficients of conditional cumulants satisfy a closed finite-dimensional system that can be solved recursively. At each expansion degree, the evolution of a coefficient introduces a coefficient of the next higher cumulant rank, while a high-rank vanishing property terminates this hierarchy, yielding a finite triangular tower. The first layer is the Kalman--Bucy filter, and subsequent layers satisfy linear equations once the lower layers are known. To derive these equations, we establish generalized Zakai and Kushner--Stratonovich equations for observation-dependent random variables and obtain explicit coefficient equations in arbitrary dimension. The conditional cumulant expansion also determines the expansion of the conditional characteristic function. We further obtain an explicit bound on the number of scalar variables in terms of the state dimension and expansion degree. When the observation function vanishes, the construction reduces to ODEs for unconditional cumulant coefficients. Comparisons with existing asymptotic-expansion algorithms illustrate the resulting reduction in the number of ODE variables.

title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on abelian Cayley graphs
abstract: We completely classify connected Cayley graphs over finite abelian groups that exhibit perfect state transfer in Grover walks. First, we show that a Cayley graph over any finite group exhibiting perfect state transfer has valency $1$, $2$, or $4$. For valency $4$, we prove that an abelian Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $S=\{a,-a,a+h,-a+h\}$, where $h$ has order $2$, and $4\nmid |Γ|/2$. Combining this characterization with the valency-one and valency-two cases, we explicitly determine all pairs $(Γ,S)$ for which $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer. Our results extend the classification of circulant graphs of valency at most four obtained by Kubota and Yoshino [Circulant graphs with valency up to 4 that admit perfect state transfer in Grover walks, \emph{J. Comb. Theory Ser. A.}, 216 (2025) 106064] to Cayley graphs over arbitrary finite abelian groups and to all valencies.

title: On a conjecture of King-Tollu-Toumazet for rectangular Kostka coefficients
abstract: A conjecture of King, Tollu and Toumazet predicts the behavior of small Littlewood--Richardson coefficients under stretching: if $c^ν_{λ,μ}=3$, then $c^{Mν}_{Mλ,Mμ}$ equals $2M+1$ or $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for every positive integers $M$. This corresponds to the Hilbert functions of a conic, or of the projective plane. We prove their conjecture for all rectangular Kostka coefficients $K_{λ,\mathbf{a}}$. We realize them as the weight multiplicities of the homogeneous coordinate ring of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$, or equivalently the weight spaces of semi-invariants of the $n$-subspace quiver with dimension vector $β=(k,1,1,\dotsc,1)$. For a weight $σ$, we show that if $β$ is $σ$-stable, then the dimension of the corresponding weight space is at least $n-2$ when $k=2$ and at least $4$ for every Grassmannian other than $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$. These three cases are precisely when the associated moduli space of $σ$-stable representations has dimension at most two. Via $σ$-stable decomposition, the two alternatives are determined as follows: $2M+1$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, and $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$.

title: A family of algebras that connects positroids, the Theta conjecture, the Delta conjecture, and Eulerian quasisymmetric functions
abstract: We define a family of algebras $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,a,b}$ whose Hilbert series, when $n\le a+b\le n+2$, $a>0$, and $0<b<n$, enumerate certain positroid cells by codimension. Equivalently, these series enumerate certain affine permutations by length. We determine the graded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-module structure of these algebras by using exact sequences to derive an invertible recursion for their graded Frobenius characteristics when $a+b\ge n$ and then passing to the limit $a\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the graded Frobenius characteristic $\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b-1}]/I_{a+b-1,a,b};q)=\operatorname{rev}_q(ω((Θ_{e_{a-1}}Θ_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\operatorname{rev}_q$ reverses the $q$-coefficients and the specialization $(Θ_{e_{a-1}}Θ_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}$ appears in the Theta conjecture. For $a,b\ge1$, we also show that $e_a^\perp\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b}]/I_{a+b,a,b};q)=q^{\binom{a}{2}}\operatorname{rev}_q(ω((Δ_{e_{a-1}}^\prime e_b)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $Δ_{e_{k-1}}^\prime e_n$ occurs in the Delta conjecture. In the three cases $a+b-n=0,1,2$, the ungraded Frobenius characteristics agree with three families of Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, respectively. We also construct an open subvariety of $(\mathbb{P}^{k-1})^n$ whose rational Chow ring is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k}$. This variety admits a stratification induced by certain positroids. Its strata need not be affine, and their codimension generating function equals $\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k};q)$.

title: Strong NP-Hardness of Rank-2 Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
abstract: Nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) approximates a nonnegative matrix by the product of two nonnegative matrices with a prescribed inner dimension~$r$. The existence of an exact NMF can be decided in polynomial time for every fixed~$r$, and a best rank-$1$ NMF in the Frobenius norm can be obtained from a truncated singular value decomposition. We prove that computing a best rank-$2$ NMF in the Frobenius norm is strongly NP-hard. Our proof uses a polynomial-time reduction from \textsc{Clique} that produces symmetric positive-definite, completely positive matrices with polynomially bounded integer entries. The same reduction also establishes strong NP-hardness of rank-$2$ symmetric NMF.

title: Rich-neighbor 5-edge-colorings of subcubic graphs whose 3-vertices induce a matching
abstract:
Let $\varphi$ be a proper edge-coloring of a graph $G$. An edge is called rich if all edges adjacent to it receive pairwise distinct colors. The coloring $\varphi$ is a rich-neighbor edge-coloring if every non-isolated edge is adjacent to a rich edge. Petruševski and Škrekovski introduced this notion as a relaxation of strong edge-coloring and conjectured that every connected subcubic graph other than $K_4$ admits a rich-neighbor $5$-edge-coloring.
  We establish the conjectured bound for every subcubic graph $G$ satisfying $Δ(G[V_3])\leq 1,$ where $V_3$ is the set of vertices of degree $3$ in $G$. Equivalently, the $3$-vertices of $G$ induce a matching together with isolated vertices. This extends the result of Chen, Tan and Zhou for subcubic graphs with no adjacent $3$-vertices.

title: Surjective maps preserving quasi-nilpotence of products of operators
abstract:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space and let $\mathcal B(X)$ the full algebra of all bounded linear operator on $X$. In this paper, we give a complete characterization of surjective maps $φ:\mathcal B(X)\to\mathcal B(X)$ satisfying \[ r(AB)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r(φ(A)φ(B))=0 \qquad(A,B\in\mathcal B(X)). \] Without assuming additivity, injectivity, or continuity, we show that there exists a function $γ: B(X)\mapsto \C \setminus\{0\}$ such that the map $φ$ takes one of the following forms:
  1. there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X\to X$ such that : \label{eq:direct} φ(A)=γ(A)SAS^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X),
  2. the space $X$ is reflexive and there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X^*\to X$ such that \label{eq:dual} φ(A)=γ(A)SA^*S^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X).

title: Generalized Cluster Algebra Homomorphisms Induced by Cluster Tube Embeddings
abstract: We relate multiplication formulas for regular modules in coefficient-free acyclic affine cluster algebras with skew-symmetric exchange matrices to the imaginary exchange relations of Reading-Stella. Introducing a parameter $z$ into the construction of Zhou-Zhu, we define a weighted cluster character on cluster tubes that satisfies generalized exchange relations of type $C_{n-1}$ and yields a bijection between indecomposable rigid objects and cluster variables. Using the multiplication formulas and difference property of Ding-Xiao-Xu, we show that non-homogeneous tube embeddings induce injective homomorphisms into ordinary affine cluster algebras under $z\mapsto X_δ$. Comparison with Reading-Stella's relations identifies $X_δ$ with the corresponding theta function, giving a representation-theoretic interpretation of the generalized exchange parameter.

title: Extremals for linear functionals on $H^p$ are outer when $0<p<1$
abstract: Let $L$ be a nontrivial bounded linear functional on the Hardy space $H^p$ of the unit disc. We prove that if $0<p<1$ and if $f$ in the unit sphere of $H^p$ satisfies $L(f)=\|L\|$, then $f$ is an outer function. The proof is short and relies on a construction due to de Leeuw and Rudin. Our result complements work of Duren, Romberg, and Shields on the failure of the Hahn--Banach theorem for $H^p$. When applied to the special case $L_k(f) = f^{(k)}(0)/k!$ for $k=1,2,3,\ldots$, it resolves two conjectures of the first-named author and Saksman and one conjecture of Suffridge.

title: Pseudoconvex domains in complex Euclidean space with one-dimensional Bergman spaces
abstract: For any $n \geq 2$, we construct a pseudoconvex domain in $\C^n$ such that the Bergman space is one-dimensional. This disproves Wiegerinck conjecture.

title: On a critical curl-curl system of Lane-Emden type
abstract:
We study the system $

We prove the existence of a ground state solution by reducing the system to a quasilinear fourth-order curl-curl equation and minimizing the associated Sobolev-curl quotient. A concentration-compactness argument shows there are finitely many concentration points for a Palais-Smale sequence $(u_n)$. This yields a.e. convergence of $

If $p=q$, we show $u$ and $v$ are necessarily equal for every solution. In an appendix we show that our concentration argument also applies to a scalar quasilinear fourth order equation.

title: Fisher Information and Support Complexity of Gaussian Mixtures
abstract:
We study lower bounds on the Fisher information of Gaussian location mixtures and their applications to estimation problems. First, for a discrete mixing distribution, we derive a universal positive-semidefinite lower bound on the Fisher information matrix in terms of the Rényi entropy of order two. For a mixing distribution supported on $K$ points, this bound scales as $\log(K)/K^2$, improving by a logarithmic factor on the support-size dependence obtained from Stam's inequality. We then develop dimension-aware trace bounds using classical Sobolev inequalities. These bounds are expressed in terms of Sibson's $α$-mutual information and yield the scaling $K^{-2/n}$ in dimension $n$. A complementary bound involving the $α$-mutual information of order $1/2$ is obtained using the sharp Young convolution inequality.
  The derived inequalities are further specialized to rotationally invariant mixing distributions supported on discrete spherical shells. In this setting, an intrinsic-dimensional bound on Sibson mutual information leads to lower bounds on the Fisher information in terms of the number of occupied shells. As applications, we study least favorable priors for bounded Gaussian mean estimation. In the scalar case, we show that the least favorable prior on $[-R,R]$ has at least $Ω(R\sqrt{\log R})$ support points and that each of its probability masses is of order at most $1/R$. In the vector case, we show that the number of occupied shells grows at least linearly with $R$. Finally, Brown's identity and the I-MMSE relationship are used to translate the Fisher-information inequalities into upper bounds on the MMSE and mutual information.

title: Graphs with three eigenvalues from group divisible designs
abstract: We construct biregular graphs with three distinct eigenvalues from semiregular group divisible designs. For every prime power $q$, we use the spectral structure of Muzychuk's Construction~A on $q+1$ copies of $\operatorname{AG}(2,q^2)$ to produce suitable group divisible designs. The resulting biregular graphs have $2q^5+q^4+q^2$ vertices and distinct eigenvalues $q^5+q^3+q^2$, $q^2$, and $-q^2$. Their coherent closures have rank $12$ and type $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&2\\2&5\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. We also determine the four-class symmetric association schemes that are the coherent closures of the auxiliary graphs in this family. Computational searches provide further graphs on $81$ and $156$ vertices, using Muzychuk's Construction~B and a generalised quadrangle, respectively; their coherent closures have ranks $13$ and $10$. The $156$-vertex example has a strongly regular design as its coherent closure, of type $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&2\\2&3\end{smallmatrix}\right]$, answering a question of the authors. We also realise a $126$-vertex example by switching a strongly regular graph.

title: Optimizers for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality
abstract: The finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality provides an estimate on the Riesz sum of the first $N$ negative eigenvalues of the fractional Schrödinger operator $(-Δ)^s-V$ in terms of the $L^{γ+\frac{d}{2s}}(\mathbb R^d)$ norm of the potential $V$, where the Riesz exponent $γ>\max\left\{0,1-d/(2s)\right\}$. We prove the existence of optimizers for every finite rank by establishing a result on the spectrum in the case of dichotomy. We further characterize the spectral gap and qualitative properties of optimizers, including the Euler--Lagrange equation, regularity, and asymptotic behavior at infinity. In particular, under the condition $γ+{d}/{(2s)}\geq 3+{4s}/{d}$, we show that all normalized maximizing sequences are precompact modulo translations. Moreover, we derive a strict binding inequality for the optimal constants in the finite-rank setting, which implies that the optimal fractional Lieb--Thirring constant, if it exists, cannot be attained by a potential with finitely many negative eigenvalues.

title: Boundary Harnack inequalities for the fractional $p$-Laplacian in Reifenberg flat domains
abstract: We prove a scale-invariant boundary Harnack inequality and Hölder continuity up to the boundary of quotients of positive fractional $p$-harmonic functions in Reifenberg flat domains with sufficiently small flatness constant, for $0<s<1$ and $2\le p<2/(1-s)$. The solutions are globally nonnegative, vanish on a common exterior boundary patch, and belong to the natural local energy and $(p-1)$-tail class. Their distant exterior values may be unrelated and unbounded. After normalization at a corkscrew point, the comparison and Hölder constants depend only on $n,s,p$. We first establish local half-space boundary comparison for every $p\ge2$ and prove relative approximation by the half-space profile in Reifenberg domains. The compactness argument identifies escaped exterior mass and excludes its constant source term. Interior $C^{1,α}$ regularity then yields gradient non-degeneracy and lower increment bounds in a cone of directions. To treat the degenerate kernels produced by linearization, we develop estimates for weighted non-local forms and prove a localized Harnack inequality for bounded quotients, retaining the full exterior interactions. Ordered variational deformations and a common fractional $p$-harmonic majorant yield comparison for solutions with unrelated exterior data. Truncation of distant data and fractional $p$-harmonic replacement extend the estimates from the variational energy class to the natural tail class.

title: Data-driven Smooth-to-hard Spectral Regularization for General Linear Inverse Problems
abstract: The logistic smooth-to-hard shrinker is the proximal map of an explicit saturating spectral penalty for general linear inverse problems. Its exact weak convexity yields a unique scaled update and proximal-gradient stationarity guarantees, while independent validation provides finite-grid parameter-selection control. We use MRI as an illustrative example.

title: Visible parts and projections of the affine fractal percolation
abstract: We study the visible parts and orthogonal projections of the affine fractal percolation. We show that for the affine fractal percolation $E$, conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, almost surely the dimension of the visible part is equal to $\min\{1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ from all directions except for the major contracting direction. The visible part from the major contracting direction is notably different from the other directions, and we provide a formula for its Hausdorff and box dimensions. In addition, we show that almost surely conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, $\dim_{\rm H} π(E) =\min\{ 1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ for every orthogonal projection $π$ excluding the one onto the major contracting direction, and given $\dim_{\rm H} E >1$, these projections contain intervals.

title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
abstract: A fusion ring is said to be vanishing if one of its multiplication matrices has determinant zero. We classify all vanishing fusion rings of rank four. We then provide a more explicit classification in the integral case, which allows us to derive several new consequences: there are infinitely many nonisomorphic simple integral vanishing fusion rings of rank four and no simple integral fusion ring of rank four is either $1$-Frobenius or Burnside.

title: Uniform estimates for elliptic systems with critical Sobolev coefficients
abstract: The $W^{1,p}$ estimate for uniformly elliptic operators of divergence form with VMO coefficients is classical. In particular, this provides $W^{1,p}$ estimates for elliptic operators with coefficients in $W^{1,n}$. However, this theory does not yield constants in the estimates controlled by the $W^{1,n}$ norm of the coefficients, since the total $W^{1,n}$ norm does not control the rate of decay for the mean oscillation. In this work, we establish uniform estimates for divergence-form elliptic systems whose coefficients lie in the critical Sobolev--Lorentz spaces $W^{1,(n,s)}$ with $1\le s<\infty$, have an $L^\infty$-bounded spatially symmetric part, and satisfy an integral ellipticity condition. The constant in the estimate is controlled by the corresponding norms of coefficients and the ellipticity constant.

title: On exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients
abstract: Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|\leq1}$ be multiplicative, and suppose that $α$ has a rational approximation $a/q$ with $|α-a/q|\leq 1/(qx)$ and $q\leq x/((\log x)^2(\log\log x)^3)$. We prove that $\left|\sum_{n\leq x}f(n)e(nα)\right|\leq \left(\frac4{\sqrt6}+o(1)\right)\frac{x}{\sqrt q} +O\left(\frac{x}{\log x}\right)$, whereas complete multiplicativity improves $4/\sqrt6$ to $1$. Both constants are optimal. In particular, this confirms a folklore conjecture on exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients motivated by the work of Montgomery and Vaughan (1977). We also obtain logarithmically weighted estimates and give counterexamples to related conjectures.

title: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
abstract: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.

title: Minimizing Age of Incorrect Information in Pull-Based Remote Estimation of a Markov Source
abstract: In this paper, we consider a discrete-time pull-based remote estimation system involving an information source and a remote monitor where the information source is a finite-state irreducible discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC) process. In this system, the remote monitor sends a pull request towards the source which responds by sampling its process so as to transmit the sampled values towards the monitor through a delay channel, encapsulated in information packets. We consider i) zero delay (ZD) and ii) unit delay (UD) channels, where the packet transmission times are zero and one slot, respectively. For remote estimation, we use the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator, and for quantifying its performance, we use the mean age of incorrect information (MAoII) which is a recently proposed freshness and mismatch metric that penalizes an incorrect estimation along with its duration. Our goal is to obtain pull policies so as to minimize MAoII under a long-run sampling rate constraint. For the ZD model, we propose a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) formulation of the problem, which allows us to find the optimum observation-dependent pull policy. On the other hand, the UD channel prevents the monitor from possessing perfect information on the actual AoII process at any given time, and the SMDP formulation of the ZD channel cannot readily be used for the UD model. For the system with the UD channel, we first provide a numerical algorithm to calculate the MAoII and the average sampling rate for a given observation-dependent pull policy. For the optimization of the underlying remote estimation system, we use the joint distribution of the age and source processes to be obtained from the history of all observations, termed as belief. Subsequently, we propose a belief-dependent policy obtained via the belief-MDP formulation and a constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) algorithm.

title: Real-Arithmetic Sketched Eigensolvers for Symmetric Matrices
abstract: In this work, we develop sketched variants of subspace iteration and TraceMIN, called sSI and sTraceMIN, for real symmetric eigenvalue problems by combining basis whitening with the sketched Rayleigh-Ritz (sRR) procedure. The nonsymmetric projected matrix in sRR may have nonreal eigenpairs, leading to complex arithmetic and additional computational costs. We overcome this difficulty using a real Schur formulation of sRR that keeps the iterations in real arithmetic. We further develop procedures for characteristic subspace selection and convergence monitoring within this formulation. On the theoretical side, we discuss suitable subspace embedding assumptions for sketched eigensolvers that use a fixed sketching matrix throughout the iterations. Under a mild embedding assumption, we establish local convergence results for sSI and sTraceMIN. Numerical experiments demonstrate runtime savings of up to 39% for sSI and 21% for sTraceMIN relative to their standard counterparts on the test problems.

title: Deterministic Determination of Axial Constants, Sectional Regularities and Annihilator Numbers
abstract:
Axial constants and sectional regularities are recently introduced
  invariants of homogeneous polynomial ideals that, like the already
  earlier introduced annihilator numbers, depend on generic choices of
  coordinates. We provide effective characterisations of the genericity
  underlying these invariants in terms of $β$-maximal position and
  strong stability. In particular, we show that $β$-maximal position
  suffices for determining generic annihilator numbers and sectional
  regularities, while its combination with strong stability yields
  corresponding results for axial constants. We also develop
  deterministic linear algebra procedures for detecting the required
  generic positions and for computing these invariants.

title: An infinite completely normal basis theorem
abstract: Let $L/K$ be an arbitrary Galois extension with group $G$, equipped with the Krull topology. Let $C(G,K)$ denote the $K$-vector space of continuous functions $G\to K$, with $K$ discrete and $G$ acting by left translation. We prove that there exists a $G$-equivariant $K$-linear isomorphism $\varphi:C(G,K)\to L$ such that, for every open subgroup $H$ of $G$, the map $\varphi^H:C(H,L^H)\to L$ induced by extension by zero and extension of scalars is an $H$-equivariant $L^H$-linear isomorphism. This gives a completely normal analogue of Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem; the case of finite base fields was previously established in an equivalent form by Hachenberger.

title: Design of a Family of Rate-Adaptive LDPC Convolutional Codes with Short Constraint Length
abstract: This paper studies the design of some high-rate, adaptive, low-density parity-check (LDPC) convolutional codes with short constraint length, based on interleaved parity-check polynomials. Starting from some known results regarding the selection of polynomials that yield codes free of short cycles in the associated Tanner graphs, we propose some new constructions based on Golomb rulers, along with relaxed variants that do not strictly satisfy the Golomb ruler condition, but retain similar structural properties. The result is a family of rate-adaptive code constructions with code rates of the form $R=(n_0-1)/n_0$. Conditions for the absence of length-4 cycles are derived, together with upper bounds on the free distance that are met in all considered examples.

title: Gradient-Hessian Query Tradeoffs: Matching Lower Bounds in Logarithmic Dimension
abstract: We establish matching lower bounds for the tradeoff between gradient and Hessian queries in nonconvex optimization with Lipschitz Hessian. In normalized units, the initial objective gap is at most $T$, the Hessian Lipschitz constant is at most one, and the target gradient norm is one. For sufficiently large $T$, dimension $d \ge C\log(2+T)$, and a prescribed Hessian budget $h \ge 1$ with $h+1 \le aT$, every randomized algorithm requires $Ω(\min\{Td^{1/3}, T^{3/2}/\sqrt{h+1}\})$ ordinary queries. An ordinary query returns the value and gradient; a Hessian query returns the complete second jet and is charged only to its own budget. Both budgets are worst-case caps. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary real points, and no Hessian-norm bound is imposed. The hard input law consists of fixed, globally $C^3$, coercive functions. The construction combines sequential readouts of a continuous random matrix with localized completion blocks and reliability dimensions that vary across hierarchy levels. Premature disclosures are charged by their expected task cost, while every oracle reply remains the exact jet of the presampled objective. This yields a logarithmic dimension threshold and a depth-independent third-derivative bound. Together with a translation of the NALEN upper bound of Chen, Liu, Luo, and Zhang, the result determines the query tradeoff up to absolute constants throughout the stated range.

title: The Hopf conjecture with $T^3$-symmetry
abstract: We prove that any closed even-dimensional manifold with positive sectional curvature admitting an isometric action by a 3-torus has positive Euler characteristic. We also prove the result for orbifolds.

title: Segal's semigroup, Virasoro structure, and Ward identities in Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory
abstract: Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory (CILT for short) is a probabilistically constructed Conformal Field Theory (CFT), expected to have connections to minimal models, Coulomb gas integrals, and loop models. In this paper, we study the quantization of Segal's semigroup given by CILT. Each element $\mathbf T_f$ in the quantized semigroup corresponds to a conformal annulus: the unit disk $\mathbb D$ with $f(\mathbb D^\circ)$ removed, where $f:\mathbb D\to f(\mathbb D)\subset \mathbb D^\circ$ is a contracting biholomorphism. This semigroup encodes the local conformal structure of the CFT, in particular the Virasoro symmetry with central charge $<1$ for CILT. We first relate the quantized Segal's semigroup to Segal's amplitudes of annuli and recover the Virasoro generators $\mathbf L_n,\widetilde{\mathbf L}_n$ ($n\geq0$) of CILT as generators of this semigroup. Compared to the real Liouville CFT, the main difficulty here is the absence of positivity, which we address through estimates for the imaginary Gaussian Multiplicative Chaos and non-self-adjoint operators. Using Segal's gluing axiom as in the real case, we differentiate the amplitude and use conformal covariance to derive the Ward identities in terms of all Virasoro operators $\mathbf L_n,\widetilde{\mathbf L}_n$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$). We also outline the parallel theory for Boundary CILT (BCILT), concerning Segal's semigroup of semiannuli. These results provide essential tools for the conformal bootstrap program of (B)CILT, boundary BPZ equations, boundary structure constants, and the global construction of conformal blocks.

title: Gluing weak approximability along recollements
abstract: We study whether weak approximability glues along recollements of triangulated categories that are compactly generated by a single object. This is applied to derived categories of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology and prescribed support for quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces.

title: Wild number for spanning trees in complete and complete bipartite graphs
abstract: Given an edge-colored graph, the wild number measures how close the graph is to having a spanning tree in every color. We investigate this parameter for complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs, with particular emphasis on minimum proper colorings and equitable $2$-colorings. For complete graphs, we determine the full range of wild numbers attainable by equitable $2$-colorings and show that, although every value in this range occurs, the expected wild number of a uniformly random equitable $2$-coloring tends to $0$ as the order of the graph grows. For minimum proper colorings of $K_n$, we establish a general lower bound, determine the exact wild number for $3 \le n \le 12$, and conjecture that the lower bound is sharp for all $n$. We also develop structural conditions on ideal wild sets and use them to obtain upper bounds and analyze the performance of a natural greedy algorithm. For complete bipartite graphs, we prove a sharp upper bound for equitable $2$-colorings and determine the wild number exactly for minimum proper colorings. Finally, we apply these results to Cartesian products of complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs, obtaining lower bounds for the wild number under minimum proper and product colorings.

title: The discrete second moment of the Riemann zeta-function along powers of Gram points
abstract: Let $t_k$ be the Gram points, and let $d\geq1$ be a fixed integer. Put $η_d=1/(2^{d+1}-2)$, $σ_d=1-η_d/d$, and $σ_d^*=7/8$ for $d=2$ and $σ_d^*=σ_d$ otherwise. We prove that, uniformly on compact subsets of $σ_d^*<\Re s<1$, $$ \frac1N\sum_{k=2}^{N}|ζ(s+it_k^d)|^2 \longrightarrow ζ(2\Re s). $$ The underlying result is a mean-square approximation by finite Euler products. For the squares of Gram points, grouping equal frequency ratios and applying the double large sieve improves the general derivative-test boundary $11/12$ to $7/8$. Assuming the Lindelöf hypothesis, both the Euler-product approximation and the second-moment formula hold on every compact subset of $1/2<\Re s<1$, for every fixed $d\geq1$. As an application, we obtain a discrete universality theorem along the same Gram-power shifts, in the same unconditional and conditional regions.

title: Barrier Log-Concavity of Large Forests
abstract: We prove that the independence sequence of every sufficiently large forest is strictly barrier log-concave: whenever $i_{k+1}>i_k$, one has $i_k^2>i_{k-1}i_{k+1}$. Consequently, every common downward coefficient tilt is unimodal, with one order threshold valid simultaneously for all $0<t\le1$. As an application, we prove that every sufficiently large well-covered tree has a strictly log-concave independence polynomial. More generally, the latter conclusion holds for well-covered forests with sufficiently large matching number. Every sufficiently large forest with a palindromic independence polynomial is also strictly log-concave, with its modes at the central ranks. The proof establishes local coefficient-curvature estimates uniformly over forests of unbounded maximum degree and over activities tending to zero. Combined with the fixed-density theorem of Fang, Lu, Nevo, Yao, and Zheng, these estimates complete the strict log-concavity interval down to rank one through $\lfloor17α/25\rfloor$; the terminal fraction is inherited. The classical decreasing tail then yields the barrier property. A cumulative-coefficient corona theorem transfers barrier log-concavity of the base forest to full strict log-concavity of its leaf corona.
